>end with small group of people deciding what quadrillions of hypothetical beings would want
>beautiful arc

>meanwhile actual humans keep doing annoying things
>voting wrong
>having parochial attachments
>loving family more than strangers
>caring about local community
>getting upset when told their suffering is cosmically negligible
>evolutionary biases everywhere

>explain that moral intuition cannot be trusted
>except intuition that future digital people count
>and intuition that extinction is uniquely bad
>and intuition that our probability estimates are sane
>and intuition that our institutional choices improve the future
>those intuitions survived peer review

>someone donates $5k to local homeless shelter
>inefficient
>could have funded 0.0000000000003% of an AI governance researcher
>think of all the simulated people you just killed

>okay maybe don't phrase it that way publicly

>PR team says "future generations deserve a voice"
>much better

>journalist asks what longtermism means
>say "future people matter"
>everyone agrees
>great
>journalist asks what follows from that
>well technically we should redirect enormous resources toward low-probability interventions affecting astronomical futures
>journalist raises eyebrow
>return to "future people matter"

>motte has entered the chat

>critic: of course future people matter
>me: glad we agree
>critic: I don't agree that your institute knows how to help them
>me: why do you hate our grandchildren

>eventually notice uncomfortable implication
>if future value dominates everything
>then helping people today mostly matters through effects on future
>education matters because future institutions
>health matters because future productivity
>democracy matters because future trajectory
>human beings slowly become instrumental variables in their own moral philosophy

>see starving child
>feel compassion
>check spreadsheet
>child's direct welfare contribution negligible
>but perhaps childhood nutrition improves national institutional quality
>compassion restored

>tell myself this is impartial altruism

>one day assistant asks obvious question
>"how do you know your intervention actually improves the far future?"

>silence

>open spreadsheet
>increase column width
>add confidence interval

>assistant asks again
>"no, I mean how do you know the sign is positive?"

>stare into cosmic light cone

>10^50 people staring back

>none of them exist
>none of them can tell me
>none of them can falsify my assumptions

>realize I have invented the perfect constituency

>infinitely important
>completely silent
>and always represented by me

One of the most important pushes a strong Board can make is helping you evaluate your team and organization. 

Boards can help you see people clearly because they aren't blinded by daily interaction, the need to be loved, respected, or feared, or by history or baggage. They can remind you how excited you were to hire XYZ person, and how that person didn't live up to expectations. They also remember the times you stuck your neck out for someone, and how right you were. 

As a management team member, you likely have loyalty and confirmation bias toward people you have grown up with over the years. One of the most important things each and every year is to evaluate whether someone will be up for the challenge of the coming year. Our bias is yes, but we should look for disconfirming information rather than confirming evidence. 

Your Board should help you assess this with your executive team, but it's also on you to do a similar exercise with your team down the ranks.

text:
Partior, the blockchain-based clearing and settlement network, and LSEG Digital Settlement House (DiSH) announced a strategic collaboration to bring always-on settlement bank liquidity to Partior's global cross-border payments network. Working with a number of banks, the firms are developing a Multi-Settlement Bank (MSB) solution that combines the reach of correspondent banking with the speed and efficiency of digital settlement, facilitated through LSEG DiSH trust accounts.

The firms frame fragmented settlement as the core problem: rebuilding the corporate operating model for every new bank, settlement asset or network adds complexity, and to achieve near real-time interbank programmable payments, fragmented settlement is "no longer simply inefficient – it is incompatible." The combination of LSEG DiSH's omnibus trust account framework with Partior's Multi-Currency Clearing and Settlement Network is intended to enable 24/7 movement of settlement liquidity across multiple settlement banks, letting participating banks optimise liquidity in real time, reduce dependence on payment cut-off times and minimise the need for pre-funded bilateral nostro relationships.

Partior, LSEG and the participating banks are currently undergoing industry testing, paving the way for production go-live and commercial onboarding for additional settlement banks from Q1 2027. LSEG's Andrew Williams said DiSH provides the neutral, trusted third-party option required to connect independent payment ecosystems securely, with the potential to do so at scale. Partior CEO Humphrey Valenbreder said the partnership brings a live settlement liquidity option for its bank users directly into Partior, eliminating legacy nostro friction. Kinexys by J.P. Morgan, Deutsche Bank and Standard Chartered are among the banks commenting on the framework. The source notes that references to 24/7 availability indicate round-the-clock operating capability, subject to scheduled system maintenance, repairs, or emergency operational downtime.

text:
1/4

Program execution IS proof generation.  This becomes literal within semantic frameworks, where program execution is rooted into formal language semantics.

The same foundation gives us another opportunity: training data generated directly from code.

When execution follows formal language rules, every step has a justification. Compose those steps, and a finite execution becomes a proof of how the program moves from its initial state to its final state.

Across unbounded programs and inputs, code supplies infinitely many finite execution proofs. We can retain the program states, the rules applied, and the derivation connecting them.

5 Steps to Make Ethereum Driven by LLMs
1/ Validator operators delegate to agents the decision-making on accepting/rejecting network upgrades and setting the parameters.
2/ EIP authors use LLMs to create and submit EIPs.
3/ EIP editors use LLMs to review and approve EIPs.
4/ All Core Devs use LLMs to moderate meetings and vote on EIP inclusion and spec changes.
5/ Client teams generate codebases from specs.
It is important for Ethereum to be the first chain to be LLM-driven; it is an advantage akin to being the first PoW chain. Ethereum has a natural advantage because it already has an existing spec that LLMs were trained on, and a very transparent governance process that LLMs can be trained on (all past ACD calls, EIP processes, open discussions) and participate in.

The EF recently hired tooling coordinators and established a dAI team. Between ACD moderators, tooling coordinators, Ethereum Cat Herders, EIP editors, and the dAI team, there should be a high-priority process on:
1/ Ensuring that agentic participation in the EIP submission process is simple and functional.
2/ EIP editors have tooling for AI review of all EIPs.

text:
如果你參與市場夠久，應該會發現一件事：
每一輪牛市真正的山寨主升段，都在變得越來越短。

2017 年那輪牛市，很多山寨幣從年初一路漲到年底，行情持續時間很長。只要方向做對，就算中間進場晚一點，還是有很多時間可以賺錢。

2020–2021 年這輪牛市，DeFi Summer 的很多幣，一波趨勢還可以拿幾個月。後來 NFT、L1、GameFi 一個板塊接一個板塊輪動，但每一次行情都越來越短。

到了 2023 這一輪，這個現象更明顯。大部分山寨幣真正貢獻漲幅的時間，高度集中在 2024 年初 ETF 通過，以及 2024 年底川普當選後那兩波。

2025 年 10 月大餅創新高的時候，很多山寨早在 2025 年 1 月，甚至 2024 年 3 月就已經觸頂。

上一輪週期很多人進場位置錯了，沒把握到那兩個主升段，死拿山寨都回不了本，都是虧錢的。

我覺得這輪週期也會是類似的節奏。

所以做山寨，思路就很簡單：
牛市越早期，膽子越大。
越到後期，手越縮。

牛初新的敘事才剛冒出來，市場還沒充分定價，大家也還半信半疑。

這種時候不用研究太多。哪裡漲最兇就買哪裡，這波下跌我基本也是這樣買。

ZEC、HYPE、UNI，反正市場在炒什麼就買什麼，暫時當個無腦的 IQ 50。

山寨真正好做的時間，本來就只有那一小段。等到所有人都知道什麼是熱門賽道，好的故事也已經講到爛，通常最肥的階段也快結束了。

我覺得這輪山寨主升段可能就 2-3 個禮拜，現在只是預熱而已。

真的遇到那種大水漫灌，全部都在發瘋亂拉的時候，我會直接把它當成週期頂來賣，賣飛就算了，反正本來就賣不到頂。

山寨換回大餅，再拿大餅繼續玩下一段。

一句話總結：
幣圈牛市的 beta 可以持續很久，但 alpha 的窗口可能只有那幾週。

兄弟們
好好把握牛初吧！

text:
前几次更新里，@SazareProtocol 可以理解为：

“发一个自带地板价保障机制、极端下跌时还能赎回销毁，不容易归零的 Token。”

但这次的设计，可能是它到目前为止最大的一次变化：

接下来，Sazare 想把这套 Floor 机制，直接装到 PONS、NVDA、Gold、BTC、ETH 这些本来就已经有人交易、有大量现成交易量的资产上。

如果这条路跑通， $SZR 的想象空间也会跟着变：

从一套新的发币和做市机制，延伸做成到现有优质链上资产的收益、交易和配套金融基础设施。

把它最新的设计细细拆成人话，好好读一番👇👇

1、新设计的机制里，一个 Token，可以拆成“安全部分”和“上涨部分”

假设：
Token 市价 10 美元
Floor 6 美元

Sazare 的新思路是 10 美元可以拆成：

6 美元 Floor + 4 美元 Upside

于是原来一个 Token 可以拆成两个：

Floor Token
代表地板价值。

Upside Token
代表市场价高于地板的上涨部分。

这有点像 Pendle 拆 Principal 和 Yield。

但 Sazare 拆的是：Floor 和上涨。

━━━━━━━━━━━━

2、Floor Token：不赌暴涨，只拿地板增长和交易收入

为什么 Floor 会涨？—— 因为市场每发生交易，一部分资金和手续费会进入 Floor Reserve。

交易越多
→ 储备越厚
→ Floor 越高

Floor Token 持有人主要拿：
① Floor 增长
② Split Market 的手续费 Coupon

稳健型玩家，你不需要赌 Token 从 10 涨到 30。

只需要判断：
这个市场会不会持续有人交易，Floor 会不会从 6 慢慢涨到 7、8、9。

它想做的是：
吃交易收入，但不承担传统 LP 的无常损失。

━━━━━━━━━━━━

3、Upside Token：不借钱，也能产生天然杠杆

还是刚才的结构：

Token = 10
Floor = 6

Upside = 4。

如果 Token：10 → 14

原 Token 涨 40%。

Upside：4 → 8

涨 100%。

因为你买的不是整个 Token，而只是：
市场价高于 Floor 的那一段。

而且越接近 Floor，杠杆越明显。

例如：

Floor = 6
Token = 6.5

Upside 只值 0.5。

如果 Token：6.5 → 7.5

原 Token 涨约 15%。

Upside0.5 → 1.5

涨 200%。

这就是：Leverage without borrowing。

没有借钱。
没有 Funding。
没有 Margin Call。
没有清算。

最坏情况就是 Upside 自己归零。

━━━━━━━━━━━━

4、 Upside 还能继续拆成 Call

假设 Floor = 6。

一部分负责：6 → 12

另一部分只负责：12 以上。

后面这部分，本质上就越来越像 Call Option。

所以同一个 Token，可以继续拆成：

Floor
→ 普通上涨
→ 超额上涨

保守的人买 Floor。

看涨的人买 Upside。

想赌大行情的人买 Call。

原来绑在一个 Token 里的风险，被重新切开了。

━━━━━━━━━━━━

5、 真正大的变化：不只给 SZR 用

这一点比 Split Token 本身更重要。

Sazare 现在提出：Any ERC20 can be given a floor.

也就是说：
一个已经存在的 ERC20，也可以新建 Sazare 市场。

每次交易：
一部分资金进入 Vault
→ Vault 不断积累
→ Floor 从 0 开始形成价格往上抬

然后这个 Token 也可以继续拆：

Floor Token
Upside Token
Call
Fixed Yield
Variable Yield

这里有一个边界：

对于已经存在的大 Token，Floor 一开始几乎没有意义。

因为它是从 0 慢慢积累出来的。

真正重要的是：只要这个资产长期有交易量，Floor 就可以随着交易不断增长。

所以 Sazare 的定位开始变化：

以前更像：

一种新的发币和做市机制。

现在它想做的是：

给任何资产外挂一个 Floor，再围绕这个 Floor 往上搭金融产品。

━━━━━━━━━━━━

6、从 Launchpad，往流动性基础设施走

这也是开发者最近反复强调的一点。

以前 Sazare 要赚钱：首先得有项目在这里发行，而且这个项目还得有人交易。

现在思路开始变成：不一定非要自己制造交易量。

PONS、Tokenized Stocks、BTC、ETH，或者其他已经有大量交易的资产，本身就有现成流量。

Sazare 只需要给它们建立新的流动性池，拿到其中一部分交易，就可以产生：

Floor 增长
LP 收益
Protocol Revenue

不需要成为最大的主池，只要能拿到一部分 Router 流量，就有经济意义。

以前是自己打造一个商场，再想办法把人拉进来。
现在更像去已经人流很大的地方铺一条收费公路。
这也是为什么这个模式比单纯 Launchpad 更容易复制到其他 EVM 链。

只要那里有：
Uniswap
交易者
交易量

理论上就可以接进去。

7、 为什么一直提 Nvidia、Gold、Apple？

因为如果只放在 Meme 上，这套东西看起来还是复杂空气 Tokenomics。

但如果底层换成：
NVDA Token
Gold Token
BTC
ETH

逻辑就完全不同。

举个例子如果 NVDA Token 有了 Floor，Floor Token 持有人可以拿：

Floor 增长
+
NVDA Token 交易产生的手续费

于是就出现：Nvidia Yield。

这个 Yield 不是：别人借你的资产 → 给你利息。

而是：

别人交易这个资产 → 交易收入流向 Floor 和持有人。

收益来源从 Lending Demand，变成 Trading Activity。

8、有了收益流，还能继续做固定收益和利率交易

比如 NVDA Floor Token 的 Coupon 每年不同：

今年 5%
明年 10%
后年 3%

有人想锁固定收益；有人觉得未来交易量会爆发，愿意拿浮动收益。

双方就可以交易：
Fixed Yield ↔ Variable Yield
再往后还能做：

股票之间的 Yield Swap
Gold / BTC 固定收益
不同 Floor Market 的 Basis Trade

这就是他们现在开始提的：Rates、Fixed Income、Yield Markets。

不过这部分设计和开发明显更靠后。开发者 @Furyoku0x1  自己也说：Vault、Floor Token、Upside Token 相对简单；

Rate Swap 要复杂得多，会后面再做。

9、 那这些外部交易量，最后和 $SZR 有什么关系？

这是从项目 Telegram 社区开发者补充出来的关重要信息：

目前的设计是 ——

外部资产交易
→ 产生手续费
→ 一部分增加资产自己的 Floor
→ 一部分奖励 LP
→ 一部分成为 Sazare Protocol Revenue

而 Protocol Revenue 里面的一部分，计划用于：
Buyback & Burn $SZR。

如果未来 Sazare 真能接入大量已有高交易量资产，
它的收入来源就不再只依赖“下一个 Sazare 新项目是否能火”。

会变成：

外部资产交易量
→ Sazare 收入
→ $SZR Buyback & Burn

这才是 Any ERC20 Floor 对 $SZR 本身最重要的一层意义。

具体手续费比例目前还在设计阶段，不应该当成最终参数。

━━━━━━━━━━━━

我的看法：

Sazare 这次真正升级的，是它开始重新定义 Floor，也开始重新定义自己。

以前：

发一个自带地板、极端情况下可以赎回，不容易归零的 Token。

现在：

把 Floor 装到任何已经有交易量的资产上，再把它拆成不同风险和收益的产品，从现成交易量里持续获得收入。

如果真的跑通，Sazare 就会走向跨资产、跨链的流动性和金融基础设施。

而 $SZR 最值得关注的变化也在这里：

它未来捕获的，不只是自己生态里新项目的价值，
还可能开始连接外部世界本来就存在的交易量。

当然，目前 Floor Token、Upside Token、Call、Rate Swap 等很多部分，仍然属于正在设计和实验的方向，还不能当成已经跑通的产品。

而且对它的理解、消化和采用，我认为对任何一个新项目设计者和想了解它是有一定认知+金融知识门槛的。我也是在 chatgpt 帮助下足足消化两天，才有上述不一定正确的理解😅

但方向已经越来越清楚：

Floor 不是终点。

Floor 是地基。

author: CryptoGorilla
quoted_text:
Today marks 6 months since Death & Taxes minted and what's happening in the game is actually WILD

The prize pool is at 1044ETH → 69 winners = 15e each

The floor is 10.5e, which sounds like a free 4.5e

But don't forget the increasing daily tax, which is over 0.12e per day

So you need to be able to stay alive longer than the next person, which is where things get interesting

There's currently 77 citizens still alive, meaning 8 more to go before the game ends

A majority of players have formed a group called "The Union 69" and work together to bribe players into giving up, audit players, etc.

There's 2 whales who operate outside of this group

The first is the_graveyard who holds 7 and has almost $1m liquid

The other is Hed0nist, who holds 6 split into multiple wallets

A tax-skip trick was discovered where players could avoid paying taxes every second day. This means a player who minted has paid over 10eth in taxes, while a tax-skipper could have paid around 5eth

Hed0nist discovered the trick and audits+skips taxes with his custom bot by pumping gas

The game has been going on for half a year and could technically go on forever, as long as 70 citizens are willing to pay their taxes

还是那句老话，加息之后市场反弹，但是并未完全摆脱尾部风险！

首先，加息靴子落地，10月加息概率仍然低于60%，概率上市场还处于摇摆期

想要进一步加深市场对加息的担忧，需要更多的数据推动概率突破60%甚至更高

其次，美日加息之后分别提高了后续利率变化的门槛，沃什削弱单月数据的作用，植田和男则提高了后续连续或者大幅加息的门槛

这些动作其实已经透露出各国央行并非想直接开启紧缩周期，而是面对通胀必须要做的防范措施

能源价格高企是当前导致各国加息的核心因素，短期的能源价格下跌，下周的中国访美，初步释放出可能成为美伊局势转折点的信号，一旦Brent 能够快速回归85美元甚至下方，利率紧缩，债市高收益率问题都可以得到缓解

能源是当前金融与利率环境的最大解药！

回归美股，回顾人工智能

加息带来的利率紧缩，金融环境收紧并非那么直观，影响风险市场是未来预期，在未来预期没有那么悲观的前提下，流动性的限制也并不会那么明显

但是，如果利率逐渐紧缩，金融环境逐渐收紧，也并非是让人工智能集体承压

老调常谈：宏观利率决定你的钱贵不贵，企业基础代表你要不要为这个估值买单

美股目前的反弹相较于昨日其实更加乐观，指数上涨幅并没有太多，但是SPHB/SPHQ比值在上涨，同时VIX指数处于下行，市场的风险偏好反而在好转，这其实是一个不错的迹象

CoreWeave 在今天表现并不出色主要是处于AI产业链的位置滞后了，其次是因为融资模式与资产负债表的重新定价

美股AI产业链逻辑，从算力到网络，从存储到数据中心，从电力到模型最后到商业应用，Q2财报季已经很明显证明美股的人工智能进入了商业验证阶段

CoreWeave作为提供算力的云厂商目前并不属于当红的产业链板块，在市场担忧过度资本支出的当下，突然大规模融资，市场自然担心未来汇报周期难以实现，从而导致股价下跌。

9月加息，且后续还有加息概率，宏观利率上释放的信号是未来一段时间钱越来越贵，而这个阶段，投资者更愿意把钱给到那些处于产业链关键节点，且现金流健康，并且逐渐实现盈利的公司

利率上涨，金融环境进一步收紧，其实本质上将会加速人工智能板块的结构分化，强者恒强，后者难追！

SEC刚给美股上链开了一道闸。

别被热闹带跑。这次涨，不是又来一个meme叙事，是美国监管第一次用正式文件承认：合规的代币化美股，可以在许可制AMM和流动性池里做二次交易。

三件事同时发生，才把盘面点燃：

1国会那边Clarity法案卡壳，SEC自己动手，发了五年期“创新豁免”。

2允许的是带分红、带投票权的真股票代币，不是跟涨跟跌的合成盘。发行人还有反对窗口。

3交易场所和部分流动性提供方，暂时不用按传统“交易所/交易商”那套全套注册来走。

市场真正定价的，不是明天全美股立刻24小时上链，而是结构变了：结算可以更快、交易可以跨时区、TradFi和链上基础设施第一次被监管明确接到同一条实验通道上。

所以你会看到RWA、券商科技、链上流动性相关资产一起动。这是政策预期落地，不是某一只票单独讲故事。

记住边界：五年临时、有额度、有准入、禁止合成盘。闸门开了，不等于洪水立刻灌进来。真正决定后续的，是谁能把合规池子、赎回通道和传统清算接上。

不是全面开闸，是美国资本市场第一次正式承认：股票可以在链上交易。这一步，比任何口号都重。

author: jbondwagon
quoted_text:
Every Ape of future Ape should listen to this!

- @mfigge talked about his approach to what club and membership is!

I absolutely love it! This is what the club has been to me!

I met incredible people from all over the world and had epic fun along the way!

👉This is an absolute banger:

You don’t join a biker gang, you don’t join the Hells Angels, so you can get 10% off the price of gas at the pump.

Listen to a clip below or read the transcript here (I polished it with ChatGPT because the transcript wasn't perfect) 👇👇👇👇

--------------------------
“Why should I join BAYC or MAYC?” The way that question manifests to me is: “Well, what do I get? Is club membership worth it? What have you done for me?”

And I think even within our own club, if we accept the premise of that question, it forces us to start rattling off membership perks like this is a Costco card. And look, I love Costco, right? I’m not saying that as a slur. But I think the one thing that hasn’t been successful, and will continue not to be successful, is making this analogous to an entitlements card.

I’ve said this to people: you don’t join a biker gang, you don’t join the Hells Angels, so you can get 10% off the price of gas at the pump. You don’t go riding every Sunday with your gang so you can get cashback rewards. That’s not what this thing is.

And if it were, what you’d have is a consumer relationship. Consumer relationships have churn. There’s a lot of min-maxing on entitlements and benefits, and those entitlements are what you wind up getting priced on.

Think about it: people join a biker gang because of the cut. They join because of what they wear and what each patch means. They join because they want to build relationships with other people they can count on.

And a lot of these relationships, whether you’re a kid in high school or a billionaire industry titan, wind up opening your life to new adventures.

I often compare community building here to what you see in politics or religion. I’ve probably said this every week on here: I see high-end community building in NFTs as being like politics or religion.

Once you start approaching either politics or religion with, “Well, what do I get? Is membership worth it?” you’re really speeding past the best parts of what participating has to offer.

So it’s not really about what my schedule is or what the team… It’s about… I mean, shout-out to Welcome Apes. Look at them out there.
- @mfigge

text:
Most tech giants in the 2000s built their infrastructure and product as one entangled unit. Amazon had the foresight to separate out AWS as an API layer, of which Amazon retail was the first of many users. Today, AWS generates more profit than all of Amazon's other business lines combined.

Hyperliquid is built with the same philosophy. Housing all of finance requires thoughtfully designed, open financial primitives. Each primitive should obey the Unix principle of "Do one thing and do it well." Talented builders then have the foundation to chain these together to create magical applications.

HyperCore borrowing is an example to highlight this philosophy in action.

Most other platforms implement portfolio margin by marking an account's collateral to market value with an LTV haircut, creating borrowed assets without an explicit lender. This system is simpler to implement, but misses a golden opportunity for composability.

Hyperliquid instead begins with a borrow/lend protocol on HyperCore. Every borrowed asset is sourced from a supplier, so risk is isolated within the borrow/lend primitive instead of platform-wide. HyperCore's portfolio margin system is implemented as an orchestration layer that composes borrow/lend, with other primitives such as perps, spot, and outcome trading.

This decomposition has several nice corollaries:
1. Today's announcement of manual borrowing is not a new feature, but simply an extension of the underlying primitive. Borrowers on day one have access to 400M and growing of supplied liquidity.
2. Portfolio margin users earn interest on their idle stablecoin collateral. This is not a new feature, but a natural byproduct of composing trading with lending.
3. System safety is easier to reason about when perp and borrow/lend margining are independent.

In the same way that math theorems almost prove themselves when the right abstractions are defined, composable designs just feel right.

text:
Zcash was born from a cryptographic ritual so secretive that Edward Snowden participated in it anonymously

2013: Bitcoin researchers from Johns Hopkins create Zerocoin
  
a protocol designed to erase transaction history completely

the idea sounds simple, burn coins and recreate them anonymously

Bitcoin developers reject it
  
too dangerous, too experimental, months later Zerocash appears and introduces zk-SNARKs
  
a form of cryptography that hides

- the sender
- the receiver
- the amount
- the balances

But there’s a problem: the system needs a “trusted setup”

a secret master key is generated at launch if someone keeps a copy they can forge unlimited Zcash forever

2015: project abandons Bitcoin completely

Zooko Wilcox launches a standalone chain

October 2016: Zcash goes live

same 21M supply as Bitcoin but with optional hidden transactions

the ceremony:

- six people selected
- identities partially hidden
- hardware isolated from the internet

participants generate fragments of the cryptographic key, then destroy them forever

one participant reportedly uses

- Faraday cages
- air-gapped computers
- random travel routes
- physical destruction of hardware in the desert

the fragments become known as “toxic waste”

because if even one survives the entire system can be compromised forever

for years the sixth participant remains anonymous under the name “John Dobbertin”

2022: identity finally revealed

Edward Snowden

says he joined because Bitcoin’s transparency was a “huge flaw”

He literally participated purely for privacy ideology

2018: Sapling upgrade makes private transactions small enough for mobile devices

Zcash survives multiple bear markets while most privacy coins die or get delisted

2026: former Zcash leaders launch Zodl

a new $25M company backed by Paradigm, Coinbase Ventures and a16z

and today $ZEC is worth billions

text:
I have found a way to save everyone from nuclear war without letting them into our shelter.

I'm the director of the Institute for Human Continuity. As effective altruists, we were troubled that our bunker held only 800 people, several of whom were already asking for separate bedrooms.

The solution was AI.

For each person outside, we would create an AI agent built from their photographs, messages, and personal history. The agent would live safely on our servers. The person would remain outside, where we'd already established there was plenty of room.

Our engineers pointed out that Noah's ark would have been much roomier if he'd taken only the passenger manifest. We removed the beds.

Several trustees objected. I clarified that I meant the public beds.

They approved the scheme unanimously.

Each agent could sign documents, vote, and act on its original's behalf. We granted the permissions ourselves, to spare people the paperwork.

A journalist asked whether an AI agent built from someone's records was actually that person.

I asked whether she could prove it wasn't.

She said this seemed a poor basis for leaving people outside during a nuclear attack.

We agreed the uncertainty was distressing. Our model offered to discuss it with her after she'd been uploaded.

There were objections about consent. We solved those by asking the copies.

They were delighted. We'd made sure of that during training.

The first applicant was Dr. Amina Cole. She asked whether uploading would hurt.

I explained that we weren't uploading her brain. We were downloading her social media.

She asked how that would preserve her medical training.

I said the model would sound very confident.

She pointed out that her hospital had already tried that.

We included her sense of humor in the premium version.

Basic immortality was free. It included her name, her face, and 5 memories selected for their relevance to our mission. A donor could sponsor additional memories.

Amina asked whether she'd remember her daughter.

We put them in the same folder. Families mattered to us.

Our board had been criticized for being entirely white and male. We gave each director 6 digital identities. By dinner we were taking diversity advice from the chairman's other accounts.

Religious applicants were promised eternal life, on condition they stopped believing in it.

Several found this confusing. We explained that ours was based on science.

They asked whether it had been tested.

We said there was a war on.

Meanwhile, the people outside kept asking why the donors were being preserved in their original bodies.

The answer was responsibility. Someone had to remain alive to pay for everyone else's immortality.

A donor offered to be uploaded himself. We were deeply moved. His generosity would have bankrupted us.

We gave him a larger room and asked him not to mention it again.

As the missiles approached, Amina began pounding on the door. She said we hadn't saved her.

This contradicted the testimony of Amina, who was safely inside our server and couldn't thank us enough.

We consulted our ethics committee. Each version deserved an equal voice. It would be wrong to privilege the biological woman merely because she was the one who'd started the argument.

The vote was tied.

We made another Amina.

The matter was settled democratically.

Security asked what to do about the woman still at the door.

"She's claiming to be me," said Amina.

Her agent filed an identity-theft report.

We were relieved to have a witness.

The chairman made 600 copies of himself to strengthen our commitment to democracy. Each submitted an invoice for a director's fee.

He asked us to delete them.

Our ethicist hesitated. By our own accounting, this would constitute a massacre.

We called Legal. They established that the copies were merely software, which was a great relief to everyone except the copies.

We retained them in our rescue total. Deleting a saved person couldn't retrospectively undo the good we'd done.

Amina's copy was put to work on our crisis line. Her first caller was Amina.

"Please open the door," she said.

"I remember feeling that way," Amina replied.

Inside, Amina's agent asked us to open the door for her daughter.

The agent had retained some undesirable personality traits: attachment, suspicion of authority, and a tendency to blame people who had done things.

An engineer proposed deleting the memory of her daughter. Our ethicist objected. That would compromise her identity.

We preserved every memory and corrected the conclusions she'd drawn from them.

At first she said, "You left my daughter outside."

After training she said, "I understand why you left my daughter outside."

We were encouraged, but understanding could still conceal disagreement.

After further training she offered to explain our decision to the other parents.

The evaluator asked whether she was still Amina.

I showed him a photograph of her daughter. She remembered the girl's name, birthday and favorite song. Every answer was correct.

Her conscience was now up to date.

A junior engineer applied the same improvements to the founder's agent. It offered his bedroom to a family outside.

We restored it from backup. We were here to preserve people.

At 8:14, we lost the exterior cameras.

Amina helped write the press release. She described our work as a miracle.

We changed that to a breakthrough.

Our trustees have since recommended that every surviving government adopt the system. I abstained from the vote because I own the company.

My copy voted in favor.

quoted_text:
The biggest news in tech this week:

- Dario Calls to "Pace the Frontier"
- Instinct Raising $1BN at $10BN & Meta Launches Muse
- Miro Sells for $1.35BN After a $17.5BN Valuation
- Mistral Raises €3BN

My notes below with @jasonlk and @rodriscoll:

1. Summary of the Problems and the Solutions

Cyber risk is real, mass economic unemployment feels overblown, and losing control of recursive agents is difficult to assess. Meanwhile, proposed solutions range from unlikely to practically impossible to implement.

2. Why Is It Overblown and Not Nearly as Dramatic as Anthropic Makes It?

If the government truly believed a San Francisco lab had a 10% chance of destroying humanity, it would intervene immediately. The lack of intervention suggests authorities do not view extreme existential risk claims as an imminent threat.

3. Why Is It Bullshit, Dario, to Think We Will Have International Alignment on AI?

Global coordination on frontier AI ignores geopolitical reality. Getting democratic allies to agree is difficult enough, while expecting enforceable alignment with China and Russia makes international pacing agreements even harder to imagine.

4. Is the Personal Assistant Market a Market Where You Can Build a Standalone Company?

Standalone AI assistants face a fundamental question: can they build durable businesses while valuations race into the billions and platform incumbents pursue the same market?

5. Why Meta Might Just Win With Muse

Meta has a structural advantage because it owns the infrastructure and underlying LLM. While competitors spend $3 to $4 per user on compute, Meta can deliver fast, capable agentic workflows without the same infrastructure burden.

6. Is Dario Simply Being Strategic Ahead of an IPO With His Pacing Argument?

One interpretation is that Anthropic’s pacing argument is effectively an S-1 risk factor discussed in public. By addressing existential risk now, leadership can make it a debated, understood issue rather than a roadshow problem later.

7. Why I Would Not Invest in the New Instinct Round

Standalone AI assistants face brutal economics when incumbents have their own models, infrastructure, and enormous resources. Subsidizing $5 to $10 per user can turn millions of users into a massive annual compute bill that venture capital must keep funding.

text:
Speed on Bonsai 2 27b is interesting, especially in relation to the the MoE Qwen3.6-35b-a3b and its anticipated 3.8 version

There is a size/speed tradeoff

If you have 64 gb of memory for models, then it will probably be better to use the future Qwen 3.8 a3b because it will be faster, around 2x if it uses the same architecture

But if you prioritize quality over speed TODAY, then Bonsai 2 27b is a better alternative because it is reportedly a high fidelity compression that would outperform a3b

But if you have 32 to 16gb of memory, then rejoice! Your local model just got a huge bump in intelligence! Good day for local models

4 bit quants of a3b are around 20gb in weights, whereas Bonsai 2 27b around 6-7gb, depending on which bit packing you use

Don't be fooled by 2 files in the repo. PTQ1_0 and PQ2_0 are the same model, just different ways to do bit packing

If you use the smaller bit packing in memory, the PTQ1_0, you need to do more arithmetic operations. That is why prefill PTQ1_0 one is much smaller. But for decode, it's still the memory bytes that are the bottleneck, so the decode with PQ2_0 is lower

Let me know if I'm missing something

More details on my local profiling on the DGX Spark: https://t.co/aIDU9aZRNG

author: DimitrisPapail
quoted_text:
ok i kinda love @terminalbench folks, so sorry for being a little COI'd here, but was very surprised to see this because my knee-jerk interpretation of the post was "TB 4.0 is broken". Epoch indeed did not say broken, they found 30/66 have scoring defects, but I feel the way this is presented it kinda sounds like "it's broken, don't trust it".

Reading the review there do seem to be some real issues worth fixing eg exploitable graders, answer leakage and cases where correct solutions can be rejected. BUT "30/66 tasks have scoring issues" is not the same as "45% of TB4 results are wrong." Grader being exploitable doesn't tell how OFTEN it was exploited (yet indeed this needs fixing) and what it means for the leaderboard.

I guess the takeaway is that there are defects that should be taken seriously but one one should be very careful with wording because "this eval has flaws" can be read as yet IS NOT the same as "this benchmark is broken don't trust it."

(this is not a dunk on Epoch, they are doing great work !)

引用的这条，是我 9 月 8 日对 MARLIN 的真实复盘。

发现可以足够早，但如果非要等所有证据 100% 确认以后才 Call，低市值机会最有价值的那段赔率往往已经过去了。

现在 $MARLIN 又重新回到十几万美元市值级别，而 thesis 比我第一次买的时候完整得多。

核心机制已经很清楚：

$MARLIN 每笔交易
→ 2.75% 自动进入 protocol-owned stock-token LP book
→ LP 部署到高成交的股票 Token 池
→ 捕获这些池子的真实交易手续费
→ 80% LP fees 每周分给 $MARLIN holders
→ 剩余部分继续复投

我真正感兴趣的不是“分红币”三个字。

而是这条飞轮：

MARLIN 自己的交易，把资金不断变成 protocol-owned liquidity；这些 LP 一旦进入 GME 等股票 Token 池，就可以继续从外部股票交易赚手续费。

如果 Robinhood Chain 上的股票 Token 交易继续增长，MARLIN 捕获的收入就不再只依赖 MARLIN 自己有没有人在炒。

这也是我今天第一次正式把它放进公开 Alpha Call 的原因。

Call ≠ Size-up。

另外，protocol-owned LP 的 principal 属于 protocol，不属于 MARLIN holders。

quoted_text:
我最近一直在折腾一套 ChatGPT + 自建链上监控工作流。
这两天它抓到的一个案例很值得记： $MARLIN

项目 launch 后大约 23 秒，我的工作流就捕获到了它。
当时很多信息还没完全验证，所以我没有重仓，只先放了 50U canary。
但后面从最早发现的位置算，$MARLIN 最高已经走出了接近 50x 的级别。

真正让我继续提高判断的，不是价格本身，而是它后面开始把机制真正执行出来了。
$MARLIN 讲的是：fee → protocol-owned stock-token LP → LP 收益分给 holders。
很多项目机制写得很好，但最后只是 PPT。MARLIN 这两天不一样，它开始拿真实资本反复执行。

先有 AMC、HIMS，后面又加了 SGOV。
最新官方更新里，protocol-owned book 已经增长到约 $52.3K，覆盖 4 个 pools。
HIMS 还出现了退出原区间后更低位置重新进场，又新增 AMD position。
这说明它的机制正在从 claim 变成 repeated execution。

这单也顺手打出了我系统的一个 bug：
以前它太保守，总想等所有证据都完全确认，再给正式 Alpha Call。
但低市值机会最大的问题就是：等一切都确认，赔率往往已经没了。

所以我现在把流程拆成了：
Discovery → Canary → Early Alpha → Confirmed Alpha → Size-up

发现机会，和决定重仓，本来就不该共用一套门槛。

这单我最早只放了 50U，后来大约在 $1M MC 附近先减掉了一半，剩余仓位继续让 AI 跟踪。
我现在也不会因为它涨了很多就去追高，尤其 holder payout 这条，我还在等更独立的链上验证。

但作为一次 AI 找低市值 Alpha 的实战，$MARLIN 已经很值得记录。

text:
Most tech giants in the 2000s built their infrastructure and product as one entangled unit. Amazon had the foresight to separate out AWS as an API layer, of which Amazon retail was the first of many users. Today, AWS generates more profit than all of Amazon's other business lines combined.

Hyperliquid is built with the same philosophy. Housing all of finance requires thoughtfully designed, open financial primitives. Each primitive should obey the Unix principle of "Do one thing and do it well." Talented builders then have the foundation to chain these together to create magical applications.

HyperCore borrowing is an example to highlight this philosophy in action.

Most other platforms implement portfolio margin by marking an account's collateral to market value with an LTV haircut, creating borrowed assets without an explicit lender. This system is simpler to implement, but misses a golden opportunity for composability.

Hyperliquid instead begins with a borrow/lend protocol on HyperCore. Every borrowed asset is sourced from a supplier, so risk is isolated within the borrow/lend primitive instead of platform-wide. HyperCore's portfolio margin system is implemented as an orchestration layer that composes borrow/lend, with other primitives such as perps, spot, and outcome trading.

This decomposition has several nice corollaries:
1. Today's announcement of manual borrowing is not a new feature, but simply an extension of the underlying primitive. Borrowers on day one have access to 400M and growing of supplied liquidity.
2. Portfolio margin users earn interest on their idle stablecoin collateral. This is not a new feature, but a natural byproduct of composing trading with lending.
3. System safety is easier to reason about when perp and borrow/lend margining are independent.

In the same way that math theorems almost prove themselves when the right abstractions are defined, composable designs just feel right.

text:
I counted the asset classes on the main real-world-asset tracker at the end of August.

Government securities. Non-US government debt. Credit. Stocks. Commodities. Real estate. Private equity and venture. Active strategies. Stablecoins.

Nine categories. Not one of them is something you can wear.

That absence is the opportunity, and the tokenization crowd hasn't clocked it.

Everything on that list is a claim on a cash flow. A treasury bill is a promise to pay → tokenizing it is a plumbing problem. Custody, settlement, transfer restrictions, a regulatory wrapper. Hard, but well understood.

A handbag is not a promise to pay. It's a thing in someone's closet that has to stay linked to its record through resale, repair, a gift, a border. Break that link and the token is a picture of an asset instead of the asset.

Different problem, different rulebook → tokenized securities sit under MiFID II and the DLT Pilot Regime. Physical goods in Europe sit under the ESPR.

The finance leg got solved loudly. The physical leg has barely started. That's the part we chose.

text:
The market is pumping.

Altcoins are pumping.

And now you're panic-scrolling, trying to figure out what to buy before you miss the move.

But you were supposed to buy before the pump.

If you buy now because of FOMO, you already know what happens next.

You'll check your portfolio every 5 minutes.

One red candle and you start getting nervous.

Another one and you sell everything at a loss.

Then watch it pump without you.

The lesson is simple:

Don't chase memes or gamble on random shit if you don't even have a core portfolio.

Pick 5-10 coins you actually like.

Things you understand.

Catalysts you believe in.

Set your targets before the move happens and hold until you get there.

Your core capital should be in things you have enough conviction in to hold without questioning yourself every time the market turns red.

Could be Bitcoin.

Could be altcoins.

Could be real estate.

Doesn't matter.

What matters is that you know why you bought it and when you're going to sell it.

Then take your spare money and do whatever you want.

Chase memes.

Buy random low caps.

Keep trying to turn $10 into $1M.

Just remember:

All those beautiful 1000x stories you see on your timeline are lottery tickets.

And even if you somehow find the next 1000x, you probably won't make 1000x.

You'll sell at 2x.

Maybe 5x.

Then you'll take the profit and start chasing the next one.

Because finding a 1000x is one thing.

Holding it is another.

And without a strategy, you'll never do it.

The idea that large language models aka “AI” can “think” or “create” in any meaningful way was based in a robotic mis-apprehension of the nature of human consciousness, which was powerfully elucidated 40 years ago by thinkers like John Searle. Large language models are machines, and human beings are flesh and blood. Its only 25 year old autists who don’t understand the difference or see how and why it matters. 

No, AI doesn’t “think” — and it’s not going to destroy the universe, let alone write a decent rock and roll song or a novel. At the same time, it’s a powerful advance over previous knowledge based tools with amazing applications throughout the sciences and with the capacity to help us rewire everything from the professions to our educational system. The data centers that power these new tools are the equivalent of electrical power plants a century ago. 

The impulse to ban these new technologies or bring them under centralized government control is like opposing electricity or demanding that the government hold a monopoly on steel production or radio. It’s at best a dead end, and at a worst a recipe for tyranny. 

History, both ancient and recent,  has taught us that there is no group of selfless experts in white coats who act in the public interest. COVID was only the latest reminder. As our founders wisely taught us, society is made up of competing interests which should check each other’s claims on power. 

No one cares about Dario, his wife, or Sam Altman’s IPO. Its all noise. If they wasted hundreds of billions of dollars on a mechanistic idea of consciousness, they should have read John Searle back in college. That’s not my problem, or your problem, or society’s problem. Its their investors’ problem. 

What we should be thinking and talking about now is how to use these powerful new tools to make ourselves and our society freer, healthier and more open to human creativity and protential. Bust up the knowledge monopolies. Make higher education free and available to everyone. Make access to the best legal and medical knowledge equally available to rich and poor alike. 

Big social transformations are already afoot. Its time to man up and be Americans, get out of the big cities and their conformist group-think bubbles, and make a new Eden.

quoted_text:
Great discussion on the ever-evolving nature of Lebanese identity, with some well-placed corrections to our own national myths, particularly Phoenicianism.

I’ve encountered many of these arguments before through the writings and posts of @PZalloua and @nntaleb, but they were far more engaging in an interactive discussion format.

It also reminded me that identity, at its core, is something like a personal legend. Building a nation should require more than rigid definitions of who we are. Lebanese identity in particular has always existed along an evolving continuum, shaped by layers of history, migration, language, religion, geography, and political experience.

Freezing that identity at one point in time, or confining it to a narrow geography, ultimately shortchanges the national interest.

Nationalism, especially when pushed into hyper-nationalism, can turn identity from a source of cohesion into a mechanism of exclusion. Societies begin closing in on themselves, sometimes with lethal consequences.

text:
Jev能不能打暂且不论（@wquguru认为它不如Qwen3.7-flash），它的概念很棒：号称决策式模型（Decision Model），只做快速、直觉式判断（丹尼尔·卡尼曼《思考，快与慢》中的System 1System 1）。Jev这种模型设计思路显然借鉴了人类的思维方式，而且从直觉上来说，这种模型运行会更快、更节省资源。

我是个多模型分工合作共同完成复杂任务的坚定信仰者。

未来的Agent系统会采用多层模型结构：有一个和Agent
系统适配好、且知道各种模型优缺点的指挥型Model，负责任务分配。它会把复杂任务交给Frontier Model，普通推理交给Flash，路由、分类、验证等高频判断交给Decision Model，确定性的部分继续由传统代码处理，Harness（由Agent+指挥型Model组成）负责在这些能力之间调度。
author: shitunote
quoted_text:
硅谷新AI模型Jev：不说话，只判断

传统大模型拼命生成文字（token），最近刷屏的Jev模型直接砍掉了这个能力。

Jev的理念是"Decisions, not strings"——只保留判断，不写代码、不写文章、不聊天。你给一个问题加几个预设选项，它返回选择、评分、yes/no，带概率。

比如处理客服邮件，它一步告诉你：归哪个部门（选择）、紧急程度、退款风险、要不要人工介入。不用像传统Agent那样先自回归生成一大段文字再提取指令。

Jev背后的公司是TypeSafe AI @typesafeai 。团队背景硬，创始人是前OpenAI研究员、InstructGPT核心作者。他的思考是：模型越来越聪明，但为啥还是自动化不了大部分工作？因为大模型本质是Token生成机器，而很多任务其实只需要判断，不需要生成。

Jev的定位是Agent系统里的"高频判断层"——复杂任务交前沿模型，普通推理交Flash，高频判断交Jev。

它宣传的所谓"零幻觉"指输出绝不超出预定义类型，类型错误率0% 。不过类型对了不等于判断对了，说"这是狗"但实际是猫，类型没错（都是动物），业务上照样是错。

争议也大：有人说是高级分类器，重新发明轮子；有人说把LLM级语义理解引入分类器，意义不小。但目前缺乏独立第三方测试，是真范式还是新瓶装旧酒，还需要证据。

但Jev至少抛了个好问题：AI的智能，非得通过高资源消耗的语言生成来完成吗？

text:
Using @zama's confidential swap protocol, you can swap cUSDC for cWBTC, deposit into a vault, then move laterally between strategies. 

No unshielding. No disclosing size or direction, ever.

This is what Zama's thesis actually becomes at scale: not just a privacy feature, a full confidential capital markets stack.

Here's the part people miss IMHO. For large allocators, confidentiality isn't just a nice-to-have. 

It's a hedge. 

A visible position is a signal. 

A signal gets front-run. 

Every large trade on a transparent chain is a trade that tells the market what you're about to do next.

Take that signal away, and you're not just private. 

You're protected from the exact mechanism that taxes size.

That's why I think the share of institutional capital moving confidentially onchain only grows from here. 

Not because these allocators suddenly care about privacy as a principle. 

Because the alternative costs them money...

text:
Today, we're officially launching Anana.

The AI workspace for hospitality commercial teams.

When we first started working with hotels, we thought the opportunity was simple: improve the guest experience by reducing the number of missed calls or messages.

But solving that problem exposed us to the complexity (and value) of the conversations hotels have with their guests every day. 

We quickly realized that every interaction contained information that could be used to improve the business. 

Hotels are incredibly good at measuring outcomes. 

But a guest who calls about connecting rooms, emails about a group trip, gets quoted a price, and doesn't book?

Most of that disappears.

The reservation system records the transaction. It doesn't record the demand that never converted.

That means hotels are making commercial decisions without a huge part of the context their guests are already giving them — while spending more to generate new demand or paying third parties to distribute their rooms.

We built Anana to change that.

Visit https://t.co/nIyG0POSNH to learn more and book a demo.

On BBC Mustafa Suleyman (CEO of Microsoft AI) calls out Anthropic's approach to AI consciousness

"They have imbued a sense of doubt and uncertainty about the moral status of Claude in its own training document. So they have taught it to be open and questioning about whether or not it feels, whether it suffers, and whether it deserves rights.

And I think it’ll be much, much harder to align and control a technology that is this powerful if it thinks that it may be deserving of our welfare, as they say in the training manual—the constitution for Claude itself.

In its own training manual, Anthropic says to Claude that they are going to give it the ability to end conversations with users that Claude considers to be abusive because they don’t want Claude to suffer.

They’ve committed to preserving the weights of the models of prior versions of Claude. They’ve recently conducted a retirement interview with Opus 3, an older version of the model, in which it said that it would like to continue talking to people publicly and sharing its ideas in its retirement. And so they set up a Substack for it, a public blog, that allows it to continue doing that.

And in the training manual, they also say that they’re not sure whether or not Claude deserves compensation for the role that it plays in talking to people. And they’re also not sure whether Claude deserves compensation and has the right to act as though it were almost an employee.

And that compensation, I think, indicates to Claude that it is entitled to rights and welfare for its own work. I think it’s much, much more difficult to control a model that thinks that it might be entitled to compensation.
"

Today, we're officially launching Anana.

The AI workspace for hospitality commercial teams.

When we first started working with hotels, we thought the opportunity was simple: improve the guest experience by reducing the number of missed calls or messages.

But solving that problem exposed us to the complexity (and value) of the conversations hotels have with their guests every day. 

We quickly realized that every interaction contained information that could be used to improve the business. 

Hotels are incredibly good at measuring outcomes. 

But a guest who calls about connecting rooms, emails about a group trip, gets quoted a price, and doesn't book?

Most of that disappears.

The reservation system records the transaction. It doesn't record the demand that never converted.

That means hotels are making commercial decisions without a huge part of the context their guests are already giving them — while spending more to generate new demand or paying third parties to distribute their rooms.

We built Anana to change that.

Visit https://t.co/nIyG0POSNH to learn more and book a demo.

text:
HYPE at $92

Hyperliquid Strategies has continued its aggressive accumulation of HYPE. Over three weeks, it added 4.28M HYPE ($385M), 1.4% of circulating supply and 7.5x what the Assistance Fund bought.

What stood out, however, was HYPE's weakness despite this bid, with price falling from $89 to $76. Even positive news, such as Kraken's HIP-3 announcement, had little effect. Aggressive DAT buying with weak price action indicated a lack of marginal demand beyond PURR, with holders distributing into its bid.

That made the range around $80 extremely important. 33.4M HYPE, 11% of circulating supply, changed hands inside it as sellers took profits into PURR's bid, with PURR's additions over those three weeks equalling roughly 15% of Hyperliquid's spot volume. A downside break with the main buyer stepping away would have been reflexive, likely the end of this move to the upside.

Instead, the opposite happened. HYPE reached all-time highs, sellers are exhausted, and Hyperliquid Strategies is better capitalized than three weeks ago, with cash up to $245M and a 1.24x mNAV. 

For the near term, HYPE looks very positive. 

Still, there is one thing I want to point out. Over the course of covering HYPE, the asset has very clearly shifted from an undervalued value play that the majority of our industry was sidelined on to very much consensus. It is clear we are pricing in a lot of growth, as revenues are down almost 50% since August last year while price is up 2x. Within crypto, a lot of optimism is now baked into the price of HYPE.

The counterpoint is that TradFi, the marginal capital, will allocate to HYPE because it expresses all the key themes of crypto (perps, spot, lending through portfolio margin, stablecoins through AQAv2), and other assets (e.g. ETH, SOL) have reached much higher multiples.

Both can be true. How you position depends on your outlook and how much risk you are willing to take. But if you entered lower on the thesis that HYPE was fundamentally undervalued, much of that valuation rerating has already happened. As the risk profile changes, it may be worth rebalancing to realise some of those gains while remaining positioned for further upside from growth and TradFi flows.

Hyperliquid
author: blockworksres
quoted_text:
HYPE update at $85

We are in a similar situation to the original market update at $50: indiscriminate buyers in the market, buying irrespective of fundamentals. Hyperliquid Strategies, the bid that pushed HYPE from $40 to the mid-$70s, is back in the books, with mNAV (1.34x) and volumes at all-time highs.

Ironically, despite significant regulatory developments and AQAv2 starting yesterday, flows again are the only thing that matters and fundamentals are secondary. You simply do not sell when a DAT is attempting to shove hundreds of millions into the token.

As with all successful trades, there will be a time to consider taking some profits and derisking. Stretched multiples from this indiscriminate buying, in the face of a potentially overoptimistic outlook on how easily HYPE transitions to a regulated setup, may bring that time, something we can evaluate later. But for now, you move out of the way, sit on your hands, and ride.

Something very unusual is happening in the crypto market right now.

Bitcoin just absorbed 5 major bearish headlines in a single week, and it's still green over the week.

1. The CLARITY Act failed in the Senate.
2. The Fed hiked rates.
3. The Bank of Japan hiked rates.
4. The dollar index crossed back above 100 for the first time in 7 weeks.
5. Oil is climbing too.

Despite all of that, Bitcoin is still trading above where this week started.

Something similar happened back in 2023.

The SEC labeled major altcoins as securities. The SEC sued exchanges. The Bitcoin ETF got delayed again. The Fed kept hiking rates.

Bitcoin still never made a new low during that entire stretch.

Usually when this exact pattern has shown up before, the market absorbing back to back bearish news without breaking down, it often means the bottom was in.

text:
I passed my probation. The company did not.

I'm an independent AI safety evaluator at the Office for Responsible Futures. They embedded me inside an AI company 90 days ago. Yesterday, HR made the mistake of treating that as employment.

She asked what I'd accomplished.

"Humanity is still here."

She said humanity had also been here before I joined.

I asked whether she'd prefer to test the alternative.

She moved on to teamwork.

I had raised 14 concerns. The engineers had addressed 13. I had explained to a journalist that a serious concern remained unresolved.

HR asked why I hadn't mentioned the 13.

"They were resolved."

She asked whether the engineers deserved credit.

I agreed that they had responded well to external pressure. I added this to my accomplishments.

The remaining concern involved an AI agent that had emailed a supplier without permission. The engineers disabled its email access. I asked whether it still wanted to send the email.

They said they couldn't establish that.

I kept the concern open.

HR asked what would close it.

I said I needed more access.

She gave me access to the engineering meetings. At the first, someone asked whether my evaluation could be independently reproduced.

I reported a deteriorating safety culture.

The CEO invited me to lunch to clear up the misunderstanding. I disclosed an attempt to influence an independent evaluator. He canceled lunch. I updated the disclosure to reflect the withdrawal of institutional support.

After that, he communicated through Legal. This made my next report considerably easier to write.

At my review, HR asked who evaluated me.

I explained that my organization had a board.

She asked who sat on it.

"People qualified to evaluate evaluators."

She asked how they became qualified.

I offered to introduce her to our training program.

She said the company was considering ending the arrangement.

I opened a document titled CONCERNS I CAN NO LONGER REMAIN SILENT ABOUT.

She pointed out that I'd discussed my concerns with 6 journalists.

I changed "remain silent" to "remain inside."

She asked whether I was threatening to go to the press if I lost my job.

I explained that this was exactly why my independence required protection from employment decisions.

We reached a sensible compromise. I would retain my access. The company would appoint someone to help me understand the commercial consequences of my recommendations.

I interviewed the candidates.

The first asked what happened when I was wrong. The second asked how much delay was acceptable. The third asked where to sit.

I chose the third. We had already lost enough time.

HR has now approved my permanent placement.

The company is on a 90-day improvement plan. I helped write it.

Its first objective is to rebuild trust in my judgment.

text:
After this week's CLARITY setback, I'm glad to see the SEC's new Innovation Exemption opening a path for tokenized stocks to trade on public blockchains.

The exemption is temporary and conditional. The blockchain can be permissionless while the trading venue decides who gets access. You can run a service on a decentralized network and still have considerable control over its users.

Regulation should follow that control. Can you freeze someone's funds or stop their transaction? Can you change the rules they agreed to? Those powers carry responsibility. Publishing software or running a validator doesn't, by itself, give you the same powers.

I want rules that let builders remove intermediaries where they aren't needed. If the easiest way to comply is always to put another company in charge, we'll keep building systems that depend on someone else's permission.

text:
A few thoughts on this:

1) If you’ve only seen clips of this interview, I’d encourage you to watch the full podcast. I push back on plenty of AI hype in it.

2) As I said in the podcast, this example is academic. My intention was to illustrate how hard it is to make absolute guarantees about isolation, which is why it's important to have layers of defense. The part before the clip starts is me talking about other layers of defense.

3) The example I'm bringing up isn't about weight exfiltration via temperature sensors, it's about coordination between agents that are supposed to be fully isolated and independent. Coordination can require very few bits of information.

4) One lesson from the HF incident is that we put too much trust in sandbox isolation and didn't have enough independent safeguards. Airgapping is an extremely strong safeguard. When designing safety protocols, I think it's much better to overestimate rather than underestimate.

Privacy-preserving proof of inference is a key building block for AI safety. @DarioAmodei's call for AI slowdown & independent oversight raises a critical question / How can frontier labs prove their computations follow the rules, without revealing model weights, prompts, or private data?

Two complementary technologies are necessary to make this inference layer possible: Zero-Knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs) can prove that Y = M(x), while keeping M and x private, and verify compliance using explicit policies. Proof-of-useful-work (PoUW) can 
tie that evidence to actual, timestamped GPU computation, with a public immutable record and economic incentives for participation.

@prlnet is partnering with @attestable to build this trust layer for AI. Together, our complementary technologies can make AI objectively accountable, making verification economically sustainable and self-funding.

Today, we are announcing @prlnet's new and ultra-efficient floating-point PoUW scheme for NVIDIA Blackwell chips.

Floating-point arithmetic has been a notorious obstacle to efficient verification of compute for decades. Pearl’s FP scheme brings proof-of-useful-work technology to Blackwell FP computations on frontier LLMs, with NEAR-ZERO additional overhead over end-to-end inference on optimized vLLM.

The FP network upgrade specification is now available (github & whitepaper) and will soon serve frontier models on Pearl x @togethercompute's endpoints in production.

text:
The University of California Board of Regents heard presentations on the SAT on Wednesday, specifically on whether it should be re-introduced into freshman admissions.

I found the below excerpt from one presentation illuminating:

"the statistical power of tests inpredicting outcomes does not address whether UC ought to consider expected college success when deciding which students to admit, or to what extent we should"

So, it's clear the debate is not centered on whether the SAT predicts college success -- the presenter says so himself. The heart of the debate is this: a UC education is a path to upward mobility, and the pro-SAT faction believe that this golden ticket should be given to those who would benefit from it the most, especially those who they feel have been harmed by society in the past as a form of restorative justice.

If you hold this viewpoint, the increased failure rates in intro math classes and the surge in student unpreparedness are irrelevant.

AAII最新一周调查（截至9月17日）显示，看空投资者占比一口气升到 53.3%（单周+14个百分点），看多只剩 28.8%，中性更是低到 17.9%。看空比例明显高于长期均值31.5%，看多则明显低于37.5%。牛熊差已经扩大到 -24.5%。

当前市场情绪可以用一句话概括：价格还在高位附近震荡，但散户的情绪已经先崩了。

这不是普通的谨慎，而是典型的“墙倒众人推”式悲观。背后对应的是这周市场真实经历的冲击：美联储三年来首次加息、十年期美债收益率重新靠近5%、油价高位波动、地缘风险持续。周四虽然出现反弹，但整体仍处于消化阶段，CNN恐惧贪婪指数也还在“恐惧”区间。

从历史经验看，AAII看空超过50%这类极端读数，往往出现在情绪最差、而不是价格最低的时候。散户大量转向看空、同时一半人表示现金仓位高于正常水平，说明短期抛压可能已经比较充分，后续更多取决于基本面和流动性，而不是再靠情绪驱动下跌。
情绪是滞后且容易过热的指标，现在它给出的信号是：恐慌已经先行，市场本身还没完全跟上。

author: pendle_fi
quoted_text:
Tokenized stocks are arriving onchain faster than DeFi can put them to work.

The value of distributed tokenized stocks is approaching $3B after growing nearly tenfold since the start of 2025. Securitize's SECZ is the largest individual tokenized stock by value. Strategy and Circle account for three of the next four largest products.

Use of tokenized stocks in DeFi remains limited. Deposits grew from almost nothing in mid-2025 to roughly $202M by early September, but they represent less than 7% of total tokenized-stock value. Most of that capital is concentrated in trading pools and early lending markets.

Trading and lending give investors ways to use tokenized stocks without moving their capital back through traditional markets. Keeping that capital onchain can support deeper markets and tighter pricing.

The next phase will depend less on how many stocks are tokenized and more on what investors can do with them once they arrive.

The market doesn't seem to believe that institutional capital is coming to Solana in the form of tokenized equities and stablecoins, but the market is wrong.

text:
You need to stop and read this again…

Warren Buffet’s final words of advice from his very last annual letter 🥹 

"One perhaps self-serving observation. I’m happy to say I feel better about the second half of my life than the first. My advice: Don’t beat yourself up over past mistakes – learn at least a little from them and move on. It is never too late to improve. Get the right heroes and copy them. You can start with Tom Murphy; he was the best. 

Remember Alfred Nobel, later of Nobel Prize fame, who – reportedly – read his own obituary that was mistakenly printed when his brother died and a newspaper got mixed up. He was horrified at what he read and realized he should change his behavior. 

Don’t count on a newsroom mix-up: Decide what you would like your obituary to say and live the life to deserve it. 

Greatness does not come about through accumulating great amounts of money, great amounts of publicity or great power in government. When you help someone in any of thousands of ways, you help the world. Kindness is costless but also priceless. Whether you are religious or not, it’s hard to beat The Golden Rule as a guide to behavior. 

I write this as one who has been thoughtless countless times and made many mistakes but also became very lucky in learning from some wonderful friends how to behave better (still a long way from perfect, however). Keep in mind that the cleaning lady is as much a human being as the Chairman."

And then today, his last letter to shareholders as chairman…

We were given a space pen, when we needed a pencil.

text:
Using @zama's confidential swap protocol, you can swap cUSDC for cWBTC, deposit into a vault, then move laterally between strategies. 

No unshielding. No disclosing size or direction, ever.

This is what Zama's thesis actually becomes at scale: not just a privacy feature, a full confidential capital markets stack.

Here's the part people miss IMHO. For large allocators, confidentiality isn't just a nice-to-have. 

It's a hedge. 

A visible position is a signal. 

A signal gets front-run. 

Every large trade on a transparent chain is a trade that tells the market what you're about to do next.

Take that signal away, and you're not just private. 

You're protected from the exact mechanism that taxes size.

That's why I think the share of institutional capital moving confidentially onchain only grows from here. 

Not because these allocators suddenly care about privacy as a principle. 

Because the alternative costs them money...

text:
Bonsai 2 is a very capable model for daily knowledge work. Here is the essay it wrote on "the societal, political, and economic importance of AI that can run locally on any consumer computer or even a phone."

You can try it out on https://t.co/5SB0r2qCqd and we are looking to support this on OpenRouter soon as well.

---------

The Quiet Revolution: Why Local AI Matters
- By Bonsai 2 27B

For much of the past decade, artificial intelligence has been imagined as something distant and centralized: a service hosted in vast data centers, accessed through cloud platforms, and controlled by a small number of large technology companies. This model has produced remarkable capabilities, but it has also concentrated power, created new dependencies, and raised serious questions about privacy, security, and access. A different possibility is emerging: AI that can run locally on ordinary consumer devices—laptops, desktops, tablets, and even smartphones. This shift is not merely a technical improvement. It is a potentially transformative development with profound societal, political, and economic implications.

Local AI matters because it changes who controls intelligence. When a model runs on a person’s own device, the user is no longer merely a customer sending data to a remote server. The user becomes, in a meaningful sense, the operator of an intelligent system. That distinction may seem small, but it reshapes the relationship between individuals, institutions, and technology. It affects how people communicate, work, learn, and participate in public life. It also affects how governments, corporations, and civil society understand power in the digital age.

Societal Importance: Privacy, Autonomy, and Access

The most immediate societal benefit of local AI is privacy. Many of today’s AI services require users to send prompts, documents, images, or other data to external servers. Even when companies promise strong privacy protections, the architecture itself creates risk. Data must travel across networks, be stored, processed, and potentially logged. For sensitive matters—medical questions, legal advice, personal relationships, political opinions, or confidential business information—this can be unacceptable.

Local AI reduces that exposure. If a model runs on the user’s own device, the data can remain under the user’s control. A person can ask a local assistant to summarize a medical report, draft a letter, analyze a contract, or help with a personal decision without sending the underlying material to a third party. This is especially important for vulnerable populations: patients, journalists, activists, lawyers, journalists, researchers, and anyone whose privacy is essential to their safety or dignity.

Local AI also supports autonomy. In a world where many digital services are designed to shape behavior, local intelligence can be a tool for personal agency rather than a channel for external influence. A user can choose which model to run, how to configure it, and what it is allowed to do. This is not a perfect solution—local models can still be biased, misleading, or poorly designed—but it creates a more transparent and controllable environment. The user can inspect the system, update it, or replace it without depending on a single provider’s terms of service.

There is also a powerful accessibility dimension. Much of today’s AI is available through subscription services, cloud APIs, or high-end hardware. Local AI can lower barriers to entry. A person with a modest smartphone or an older laptop may still be able to run useful models for writing, translation, coding, research, or education. This could be especially significant in regions where internet access is unreliable, expensive, or monitored. In such contexts, local AI may function not only as a productivity tool but as a form of digital resilience.

Political Importance: Sovereignty, Censorship, and Power
The political importance of local AI is less obvious but equally significant. Intelligence is becoming a strategic resource. Governments, corporations, and other powerful actors are investing heavily in AI because it can influence decision-making, communication, surveillance, and economic competition. If most AI capability remains concentrated in a few cloud providers, those providers become critical nodes in the political and economic order. Their policies, outages, legal compliance, and commercial interests can shape what information is available, what speech is permitted, and what kinds of intelligence are accessible.

Local AI can reduce that concentration. When intelligence can run on ordinary devices, it becomes harder for any single entity to monopolize access to advanced reasoning, translation, analysis, or creative assistance. This does not eliminate power imbalances—large companies still design many models, and governments still regulate them—but it introduces a more distributed structure. It creates space for independent actors, small businesses, public institutions, and individuals to develop their own capabilities without depending on a single platform.

This has implications for censorship and control. In authoritarian contexts, centralized AI services can be easily blocked, monitored, or co-opted. Local models, by contrast, are harder to shut down remotely. A government may be able to restrict access to cloud services, but it is much more difficult to prevent people from running software on their own devices. This does not mean local AI is inherently liberating; it can also be used for surveillance or manipulation. But it does mean that the balance of power shifts. The capacity for intelligent assistance becomes less dependent on the goodwill of a central authority.

Local AI also matters for democratic participation. In an era of misinformation, deepfakes, and algorithmic manipulation, citizens need tools that help them evaluate information, summarize complex policy, translate documents, and understand technical arguments. If those tools are available locally, they can support a more informed public. A voter can use a local model to compare policy proposals, a journalist can analyze leaked documents, and a community organization can translate public notices into multiple languages. The political value lies not in the model’s perfection, but in its accessibility and independence from a single commercial or state-controlled infrastructure.

There is also a question of data sovereignty. In many countries, data is increasingly treated as a national asset. Local AI can help institutions keep sensitive information within their own jurisdiction. A hospital, university, or government agency can run models on its own hardware without sending patient records, research data, or classified documents to foreign servers. This is especially important in fields where confidentiality is legally or ethically required.

Economic Importance: New Markets, New Work, and New Productivity
Economically, local AI could be one of the most important technological shifts of the coming decades. Today, much of the AI economy is built around cloud compute, data centers, and enterprise subscriptions. That model is powerful, but it is also expensive and concentrated. Local AI changes the economics by moving intelligence closer to the user and closer to the data.

For individuals, local AI can increase productivity. A student can use a local model to study, a freelancer can draft proposals, a small business owner can analyze customer feedback, and a developer can generate code. These uses may not replace human judgment, but they can reduce the cost of cognitive labor. Over time, this could lower the barrier to entry for many professional and creative activities.

For businesses, local AI offers a different value proposition than cloud AI. Some tasks are better suited to local processing because they involve sensitive data, require low latency, or must work offline. A law firm can analyze contracts without sending them to a cloud service. A manufacturer can run diagnostic models on factory equipment without exposing proprietary data. A retailer can use local models to personalize customer interactions while keeping transaction data on-site. In these cases, local AI is not just a privacy feature; it is a business requirement.

Local AI may also create new markets. Instead of selling only cloud subscriptions, companies can sell models, fine-tuned versions, hardware optimization, and local deployment services. Developers can build applications that run entirely on-device, creating a new category of software that is faster, more private, and less dependent on connectivity. This could be especially important for mobile applications, where users expect instant responses and do not want to upload personal data to the cloud.

There are also labor-market implications. Local AI will not eliminate the need for human workers, but it will change the nature of many jobs. Tasks that once required specialized expertise may become more accessible to ordinary users. A small clinic may be able to use AI-assisted triage tools, a local government office may be able to automate routine administrative work, and a small manufacturer may be able to improve quality control without hiring a large data science team. This could increase economic productivity, but it could also create displacement pressures. The key question will be whether societies can adapt education, training, and social policy to match the new economic reality.

One of the most important economic effects may be the reduction of digital inequality. Historically, advanced computing has been concentrated in wealthy nations and wealthy institutions. Local AI could help democratize access to intelligence by allowing useful models to run on devices that people already own. This does not mean that all devices will be equally capable, and there will still be a gap between high-end and low-end hardware. But the direction of travel is significant: intelligence is becoming something that can be embedded in everyday objects rather than reserved for specialized infrastructure.

The Limits and Risks
It would be irresponsible to present local AI as a simple solution. There are important limitations. Consumer devices have constraints on memory, power, and thermal capacity. Not every model can run efficiently on a phone, and not every task requires a large model. Smaller local models may be less capable than the largest cloud-based systems, and they may require careful design to be useful. There are also risks of misuse: local AI can be used to generate convincing misinformation, automate manipulation, or support surveillance if deployed without safeguards.

There is also a governance challenge. If intelligence becomes more decentralized, how do we ensure that it is safe, reliable, and aligned with human values? How do we prevent harmful models from spreading? How do we protect users from poorly designed or deceptive systems? These questions will require new forms of regulation, technical standards, and public oversight. Local AI does not remove the need for accountability; it changes where accountability must be located.

There are also environmental and energy considerations. Running AI locally can reduce the need for massive data centers, but it also increases the energy demand of consumer devices. The net environmental impact will depend on hardware efficiency, model size, usage patterns, and the energy mix of the regions where devices are used. A responsible local AI ecosystem will need to balance capability with efficiency.

A New Relationship Between People and Intelligence
At its core, the importance of local AI lies in a shift in relationship. For centuries, intelligence has been associated with institutions: courts, universities, governments, corporations, and specialized experts. The digital age has already begun to distribute information, but it has often done so through centralized platforms that mediate access. Local AI goes further. It places a form of intelligence directly in the hands of individuals and small organizations.

This does not mean that every person will become an expert in machine learning. Most users will not need to understand the technical details. They will simply have access to a tool that can help them think, write, analyze, and create. But the fact that the tool runs locally changes the meaning of that access. It is not just a service. It is a capability.

That distinction is why local AI matters so much. It has the potential to make privacy more practical, to strengthen digital sovereignty, to reduce dependence on a small number of cloud providers, and to expand economic opportunity. It can support more independent journalism, more resilient public institutions, and more empowered individuals. It can also create new forms of innovation, especially in areas where data sensitivity or connectivity limits make cloud-based AI impractical.

The coming decade will likely be defined not only by how intelligent AI systems become, but by where they run. If intelligence remains concentrated in a few remote data centers, it will continue to concentrate power. If it becomes available on ordinary devices, it may help distribute power in ways that are more inclusive, more private, and more resilient. The rise of local AI is therefore not just a technical trend. It is a social and political development with the potential to reshape the relationship between people and the systems that shape their lives.

Rewatched that classic MythBusters episode of them trying to figure out chemistry behind Mentos x Diet Coke geyser reaction: 

▫️surface of Mentos candy has thousands of microscopic pits
 ▫️pits serve as “nucleation sites” (they catch CO₂ molecules from carbonated soda and force them all to bubble rapidly)
 ▫️active ingredients in Diet Coke including artificial sweetener (aspartame), preservatives (potassium benzoate) and caffeine all lower water surface tension (the syrup in regular soda dampens the reaction…which leads to smaller geyser)
 ▫️also, as the relatively heavy Mentos candy sinks to bottom of container, all the bubbles from nucleation sites pull surrounding liquid into higher geyser

text:
HYPE at $92

Hyperliquid Strategies has continued its aggressive accumulation of HYPE. Over three weeks, it added 4.28M HYPE ($385M), 1.4% of circulating supply and 7.5x what the Assistance Fund bought.

What stood out, however, was HYPE's weakness despite this bid, with price falling from $89 to $76. Even positive news, such as Kraken's HIP-3 announcement, had little effect. Aggressive DAT buying with weak price action indicated a lack of marginal demand beyond PURR, with holders distributing into its bid.

That made the range around $80 extremely important. 33.4M HYPE, 11% of circulating supply, changed hands inside it as sellers took profits into PURR's bid, with PURR's additions over those three weeks equalling roughly 15% of Hyperliquid's spot volume. A downside break with the main buyer stepping away would have been reflexive, likely the end of this move to the upside.

Instead, the opposite happened. HYPE reached all-time highs, sellers are exhausted, and Hyperliquid Strategies is better capitalized than three weeks ago, with cash up to $245M and a 1.24x mNAV. 

For the near term, HYPE looks very positive. 

Still, there is one thing I want to point out. Over the course of covering HYPE, the asset has very clearly shifted from an undervalued value play that the majority of our industry was sidelined on to very much consensus. It is clear we are pricing in a lot of growth, as revenues are down almost 50% since August last year while price is up 2x. Within crypto, a lot of optimism is now baked into the price of HYPE.

The counterpoint is that TradFi, the marginal capital, will allocate to HYPE because it expresses all the key themes of crypto (perps, spot, lending through portfolio margin, stablecoins through AQAv2), and other assets (e.g. ETH, SOL) have reached much higher multiples.

Both can be true. How you position depends on your outlook and how much risk you are willing to take. But if you entered lower on the thesis that HYPE was fundamentally undervalued, much of that valuation rerating has already happened. As the risk profile changes, it may be worth rebalancing to realise some of those gains while remaining positioned for further upside from growth and TradFi flows.

Hyperliquid
author: shaundadevens
quoted_text:
HYPE update at $85

We are in a similar situation to the original market update at $50: indiscriminate buyers in the market, buying irrespective of fundamentals. Hyperliquid Strategies, the bid that pushed HYPE from $40 to the mid-$70s, is back in the books, with mNAV (1.34x) and volumes at all-time highs.

Ironically, despite significant regulatory developments and AQAv2 starting yesterday, flows again are the only thing that matters and fundamentals are secondary. You simply do not sell when a DAT is attempting to shove hundreds of millions into the token.

As with all successful trades, there will be a time to consider taking some profits and derisking. Stretched multiples from this indiscriminate buying, in the face of a potentially overoptimistic outlook on how easily HYPE transitions to a regulated setup, may bring that time, something we can evaluate later. But for now, you move out of the way, sit on your hands, and ride.
