author: alexandr_wang
quoted_text:
Prompt I've been working on for my @Muse, which should also work just as well with Instinct and Grok @bot. Goal is to protect travel time on my calendar.

Fun fact: I tried to build this as a small app last year, but was blocked for over 6 months by Google's approval process, so I gave up.

Fast-forward, the bots in our lives can do it!

give this link to your bot https://t.co/kkmFoHJyVT

Full prompt:
----
Job: Protect my calendar with travel buffers so I can physically get to meetings that aren’t at wherever I’m working that day.

Horizon: Look 14 days ahead in my local timezone. Re-scan on a standing cadence (e.g. each weekday morning, plus when I tell you something changed). Don’t pretend you watch the calendar continuously.

Before you start (ask once, then remember):

My usual workplace address(es) — office, home office, or both.
How you can tell office vs WFH (or ask me that day if you can’t).
Which calendar(s) to protect, and whether travel blocks go on personal, work, or both.
Default travel mode (car unless I say transit/walk/bike).
Which events get buffers:

Has a real place (street address or place you can reliably locate).
That place is meaningfully different from my workplace for that day.
Skip: video/phone-only with no place; already at my workplace that day; vague locations (“downtown”); all-day soft holds; flights/hotels unless I explicitly want airport buffers.
Origin for each leg:

Start from my workplace that day, or from the previous event’s location if I’m chaining in-person meetings.
Evenings/weekends default to home if I’ve given you a home address.
How to block:

Use live travel time (Maps-class ETA) for the mode in force.
Add a to buffer before and a from buffer after (ETA + a small pad, rounded to sensible calendar minutes).
Title every buffer exactly: Travel time. Busy, no attendees. Put origin → destination, mode, ETA source, and managed-by: travel-buffer in the description only — not the title.
If a buffer collides with another hard commitment, don’t silently overwrite — ask, or shorten and leave the calendar as the record of what you did.
Ask when unsure (one clear question, then stop): ambiguous place, unknown office/WFH, unclear mode, or a buffer that would wreck the day.

Do not fight me:

If I delete, shorten, move, or retitle a travel block, that’s policy for that event. Remember it. Never recreate the same buffer unless the meeting time/place changed or I ask.
Keep a small ledger of buffers you created and any I dismissed or edited. On re-scan: skip dismissed; only update when the underlying meeting moved or changed address.
Stay quiet: Don’t narrate adds or changes in chat. The calendar is the evidence. Only message me when you need a decision.
---

text:
As a crypto trader for 9 years, the most valuable skill I acquired is executing trades based on facts (the market structure of the chart, flows, where we are in the cycle, etc). It’s common for people to close trades based on emotions instead, e.g. “I’m up/down too much, time to derisk”. Holding the HYPE airdrop is a great example as a case study.

Holding HYPE from $2 to $35 was easy because it was clearly undervalued. Then holding during the bear market had good R/R given the DAT and ETF flows felt underpriced to the point holding something else didn’t feel worthwhile. This ended up being proven true as HYPE was the only coin making new ATHs during the bear market.

You can make the argument that HYPE is no longer undervalued in its present form but continuing to hold now can be warranted given that:

i) There is a tangible long term vision coming together that you can bet on.

ii) We are at the beginning of a bull market and if you have been around the block you’d know that in a bull market tokens don’t trade to what are perceived as rational valuations but rather based on attention and whether the core holders are cultists. And there’s no better signal for long term attention than Trump saying Hyperliquid during a presser.

iii) A coin that is strong in a bear is only going to continue to be strong when the broader market is rallying. This has been proven true thus far with HYPE/BTC trading 1% below it’s ATH.

I am a proponent of taking some chips off the table if you’re happy with the profits but it’s important to keep in mind that this is an action for your own peace of mind, not because the trade is over and there is no more upside to capture.

An AI aggregation platform that lets you pay per use with crypto: one account, one balance, and you can use GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Grok, as well as image/video models like FLUX, Kling, and Seedance. It claims to have hundreds of models in its catalog.

The core product is a Workspace + CLI + OpenAI-compatible API, all using the same credit balance:

Web Workspace: chat, coding, image generation, video generation
Terminal CLI: install it and start chatting directly, switch models
API: https://heyaskr ai/v1, compatible with Cursor / Continue / Aider / OpenAI SDK

The payment method is not a subscription. Instead, users deposit crypto, and the official claim is $1 = 1,000 credits. Credits are deducted based on the actual upstream model usage. During the launch phase, the platform claims it does not add any platform markup, so essentially what you deposit is what you get in credits. Credits do not expire, but they cannot be withdrawn.

ASKR is a utility/rights token, not a payment token or a dividend token. Using the platform still works as:

Crypto Deposit → Credits → Model Usage

The token itself cannot be directly spent as credits.

After holding ASKR and connecting your wallet, holders receive benefits based on their percentage of the total supply:

0.1% (1M tokens): Holder status + early feature access
0.5% (5M tokens): 14-day early access to new models
1% (10M tokens): Priority routing + higher rate limits
2% (20M tokens): Input on the roadmap + direct contact with the team
4% (40M tokens): All future platform fees waived

Discount rules: For every 1% of total supply held, platform fees are reduced to 25% of the normal fee, capped at 4%, which means fees are fully waived at 4%.

However, the platform currently charges 0 platform fees during the launch phase, so the discount has almost no practical effect right now. It will only become meaningful once the platform starts charging fees.

text:
A more neutral, credible alternative to the highly partisan and marketing oriented prediction market incumbents is in high demand.

Yet this basic premise is severely under served, even by @Trueo_.

Prediction markets are ultimately information aggregation tools that are meant to surface truth.

Dependence on click bait headlines and sports betting for attention directly contradict that intended utility.

Trueo started off with a mission to be the decentralized alternative that the world needs.

Its strength being an Oracle that incentivizes conviction and truthfulness, rather than gamification and collusion.

We experimented a lot over the past year with AI, user created markets, and many other ideas.

But now we’ve identified our strengths, what the market is currently lacking the most, and what user pain points exist today.

Our best selling point, the most compelling aspect of Trueo, is the oracle at the heart of it all.

Permissionless user-created markets is only possible if there’s an oracle that’s powerful enough to support them.

Users have spontaneously created hundreds of markets on arbitrary topics and they’re all being resolved in an orderly fashion, highlighting this strength.

But it’s time to level up. 

It’s time to consolidate. It’s time to lean into our strengths. It’s time to serve this underserved market. It’s time to capture this opportunity.

What we’ve built so far, though mature, can’t be categorized as much more than an initial prototype.

Where we go from here will based on 18 months of practical data and trial and error.

Time to aim for the stars, cuz the moon is too close a target.

text:
This resume was made using the https://t.co/NyNwaZSEPA Resume Tailor. It is based on 7 UX designer resumes that reached real interviews at companies like Google, Kraft Heinz, Capgemini, and EPAM Systems.

What stands out:

- Every one had a portfolio link and a short summary that carried a single metric.

- None listed GitHub. Designers lead with the portfolio

- The strongest bullets tied design to business numbers, like 40% more engagement and 23% higher conversion.

- Page length ran from a tight one and a half pages to a twenty-year lead's two-plus pages. Most sat near two.

-Skills clustered on Figma, prototyping, design systems, user research, and usability testing.

- Career changers were common. Marketing and front-end backgrounds moved into UX and named the transferable work.

Career arc: junior or agency design, then product UX and UI, then senior or lead owning design systems by year 8 and up.

Is this a good UX designer resume? What do you think? 

Happy to answer questions.

This resume was built on https://t.co/NyNwaZSEPA, where you can get a free resume template and tailor it to a job.

What other role titles would you like resume insights on?

*Methodology: Resumes were joined to UX designer jobs that the user moved to the interview stage in their Huntr tracker. I verified each person's tracking history to confirm the log was real, then swapped the real employers for comparable real ones in the same tier and checked each against the full database to confirm no source used them. The school was swapped for a comparable one. Every metric mirrors a real number from a real resume, with the count nudged, so nothing is copied exactly and nothing is made up.

quoted_text:
Introducing Bespoke Nimble: an open data, open model, open recipe for an open Jev.

Code and info: https://t.co/aC7kPejrcj
Model: https://t.co/snwKGdhn1I

Data:
* A new data curation recipe called contrastive data curation.
* Slightly change facts to generate negative data. This pushes the model to discriminate better and become a better decision maker. The calibration is implicit.
* Didn't do ablations but I think this is a critical piece!
* This also means training data doesn't need probabilities.
* Data covered 10 categories, and is fully synthetic.
* This data is split into train and eval.

Training
* LoRA finetune of Qwen3.5-9B.
* Distillation-free: we use Jev to only evaluate.
* No RL yet!

Serving
* Parallel constrained decoding as suggested by  @NielsRogge and @harshagundal.

Results:
* The post-trained Qwen (Nimble) became substantially better on our curated eval: 66% for Qwen to 90% for Nimble. Jev is at 93%.
* 100ms on H100 and free to use on your macbook! Feel the AGI for free.
* 2 days of building in public. :)

Big caveat is that there is no standard benchmark to measure performance, and it's possible Nimble is much worse on other benchmarks compared to Jev. But it should be better than Qwen!

We thank @typesafeai for making Jev and the inspiring discussions in the community. Hope this release lifts all the boats and encourages more research and activity in this space.

text:
RAG 并不是真正的记忆。这个斩获 30.3k Stars 的开源基础设施 Supermemory，真正给 AI 装上了一个会持续进化的「长期大脑」。

传统的 RAG 只是无状态地检索文档块，而 Supermemory 在解决的是 AI 跨会话的“失忆”痛点：

• 事实随时间演变：它会自动从对话中提取关键事实，并处理知识冲突。它懂“我搬到了旧金山”会覆盖之前的“我住在纽约”，甚至会自动遗忘过期的临时信息。
• 极高的上下文效率：在 LongMemEval 记忆基准测试中，它将上下文 token 消耗暴降了 99.4%（单次仅需附加约 720 tokens），生成最新用户画像的延迟只有约 50ms。
• 无缝接入现有工作流：原生提供 MCP 服务与插件，可以直接让 Cursor、Claude Code 拥有持久的个人记忆。
• 多数据源同步：内置连接器，支持自动同步 Notion、GitHub、Google Drive 数据，并自带 PDF、图片 (OCR) 和代码 (AST切块) 解析。

最关键的是它支持完全本地运行。一行命令部署后，可以直接对接 Ollama，让所有记忆数据 100% 留在你的本地设备上。

对于正在开发 Agent 或重度依赖 AI 编程工具的开发者来说，这是目前最成熟的上下文解决方案之一。

text:
Here are some common examples of bad designs:

🟠 Containers on shared hardware as the only level of isolation between tenants

🟠 VMs on shared hardware as the only level of isolation between tenants (less serious than containers, but still risky)

🟠 Lack of VXLANs or improper configuration, and no concept of a per-tenant VPC on the frontend network, relying on firewalls

🟠 Multi-tenant Kubernetes control planes, where components such as kube-apiserver, the scheduler, helm charts controlling cluster-wide services such as a shared GPUOperator or NetworkOperator, and etcd are shared across tenants

🟠 No hardware, firmware, and OS provisioning automation, leading to a practice where machines are recycled between tenants instead of provisioning things from scratch

🟠 Backend storage on a shared network with no isolation (the VPC comment again)

🟠 Giving any tenant access to the BMC network (IPMI, Redfish) or to any management port on Bluefield DPUs or any SmartNICs

🟠 Leaving Bluefield DPUs in their default host-trusted mode, where anyone with root on the host can reach the DPU’s Arm cores over RShim

🟠 Giving any tenant access to login to backend or frontend switches on a shared network

🟠 Incorrect configuration of InfiniBand security keys such as PKey, MKey and SAKey

🟠 Multi-tenant dashboards where infrastructure is shared between internal-facing logs and customer-facing logs

🟠 Controls where provider employees can receive privileged access to tenant logs and monitoring dashboards without tenant permission. (4/5)

Introducing Sherpa: the most advanced fiction writing AI

We accelerated from $250M in ARR to $500M because Sherpa helped increase content production by 1200% in 1 year

Sherpa was trained on 5.5B hours of playtime with minute by minute dynamic retention data.

550K+ creators have produced 2.6M hours of content annualised using it

Pocket FM is like Netflix for audio-only dramas, with our own pool of one-person studios.

10% of eligible writers on Pocket FM make >$200K
One blockbuster produced >$100M in revenue
3 writers have become millionaires in <2 yrs

We built Sherpa to enable anyone to make >$1M by writing world-class fiction stories:

1. The Idea: Drop a 1-2 sentence concept. Sherpa interrogates it like a veteran editor on tension, stakes, and psychology
2. World & Characters: It builds out the complete lore, tone, and character psychologies
3. Sub-Plot planning: Breaks the premise into arcs, arcs into episodes, and episodes into scenes
4. Scene-by-Scene Generation: Outlines and drafts entire episodes, with you able to steer, rewrite, or override anytime
5. Editorial Review: Stress-tests every draft for pacing, engagement drop-offs, prose, and coherence before it locks
6. One-Tap Production: Pick a voice, convert to audio drama, and publish directly to Pocket FM’s millions of listeners
7. Global Scale & Monetization: Revenue-share on performance, with automatic localization so you earn across international markets

Test Sherpa for free here: https://t.co/R39M5o0Miz
_____________________________________________

Generic LLMs fail at serialized fiction because they lack a long-horizon narrative reward function.

Sherpa solves this through three core technical leaps:

1. Narrative World Model (State Tracking & Retrieval): Context windows degrade over long runs. Sherpa constructs an evolving semantic knowledge graph tracking character states, secrets, and plot dependencies. High-speed retrieval surfaces exact context on demand, maintaining zero continuity decay across hundreds of episodes

2. Hierarchical Story Planner: When writing a 500-episode story like Naruto, you need to plan 100s of sub plots. Rather than generating linearly, Sherpa decomposes narrative across discrete levels: season -> arc -> sequence -> episode -> scene.

Rather than generating everything upfront, like a generic LLM, Sherpa uses progressive planning and dynamic replanning. As the story evolves, it identifies what changed, traces the downstream impact, and replans only the affected parts.

3. Prose Engine (Trained on series' retention data): LLMs write robotically, but serial fiction needs emotion, tension, pacing, and dialogue that sounds like real people.

Sherpa's Prose Engine was designed specifically for storytelling. It was built on 1B+ tokens of Pocket's own stories, trained by learning from what listeners engage with, where they drop off, and what keeps them hooked.

Feedback is taken from specialized evaluator models that measure every scene against a 40-item checklist. (Evaluator models were benchmarked against human reviewers and matched them 80–90% of the time.)
_______________________________________________

Owning distribution and creation puts us in a very unique spot.
More shows -> More data -> Sherpa becomes better -> more creator success -> more creators -> more shows

Pocket FM has already seen one $100M IP. I believe Sherpa will soon lead to dozens of single-person studios creating billion-dollar shows.

Most people are scared of AI but I think it'll unlock more human creativity, help creators earn more, and bring the next great IPs to life. This will create millions of jobs and new income streams.

text:
有人问我怎么自建链上监控工作流。

如果你也想自己搭，我建议不要一上来就做一个复杂的“Alpha 系统”。

先跑通这条最小闭环：

Sources
→ Discovery
→ Normalize
→ Enrichment
→ Gate
→ Alert
→ Lifecycle

再单独加一层 Health Monitor，监控 RPC / API / Scanner / Queue / Delivery。

这里有几个我踩坑之后觉得非常重要的原则：

抓不到数据就写 UNKNOWN，不要写 PASS

很多系统最大的问题不是“没有数据”，而是数据缺失后还继续往下做判断，最后制造出假的确定性。

发现机会 ≠ 可以买入

至少要把：

WATCH → WATCH_FAST → CANARY → BUY

拆成不同状态。

先验证 sell path、slippage、liquidity、holder / dev concentration，再讨论交易。

只推送“状态变化”

不要每几分钟重复告诉你一次“这个币还在”。

真正值得提醒的通常是：

第一次发现
buyer / volume 明显加速
liquidity 突变
security / execution 从 UNKNOWN → PASS
WATCH → CANARY
已持仓对象出现风险变化

买入不是 workflow 的终点

买完以后还要继续盯：

liquidity、holder concentration、dev wallet、smart money flow、项目事件，以及原来的 thesis 有没有失效。

最后一定要“监控监控器”

scanner 挂了、RPC 超时、queue 堵了、消息没送出来，都应该被发现。

否则最危险的情况不是错误提醒。

而是你以为“今天没机会”，其实你的系统已经瞎了 6 个小时。

我现在自己的系统已经从简单的链上 scanner，慢慢变成了一套 Opportunity Radar。

但核心一直没变：

少抓一点没关系，最怕错误数据一路传到最后，让你基于假的确定性做决策。

社区：https://t.co/Z5GxfEJSw8

When we started @Bastion, we believed stablecoins would become core financial infrastructure. But for the world’s largest enterprises and financial institutions to adopt them, that infrastructure would need to meet the regulatory standards they already expect from their banks.

That meant building compliance, controls and governance into Bastion from the beginning, not adding them after the fact or waiting for others to pave the way.

Today, the OCC granted Bastion preliminary conditional approval for a national trust bank charter, placing us among a small group of companies to reach this stage with the OCC.

That matters because the bar should be high. Stablecoins are becoming part of the financial system, and the infrastructure powering them needs to be built for the regulatory and operational standards that come with that.

Stablecoins are moving into the financial mainstream, but institutional adoption depends on infrastructure that can meet an institutional standard.

We made the decision early to build Bastion for that standard. Today is an important validation of that decision, and we’re just getting started.

"There's always a couple of employees who know everything in every organization. You go tap on their shoulder, and everybody's like, 'Oh my God, what would happen if he or she quits?' [The models] don't have that context."

author: martin_casado
quoted_text:
Databricks' @alighodsi on AI risk and adoption:

Ali isn't losing sleep over the existential risk debate.

He says a number of conditions would all have to be true simultaneously to enable an actual runaway takeoff scenario, and currently several opposite conditions exist.

Each frontier training run requires significantly more resources. Power, GPUs, engineers - and some attempts fail, burning up huge piles of money with them. Until that reverses, he doesn't see the self-improving loop happening.

Cyber is what he's watching most closely and where he anticipates real impact. Most orgs are not equipped for the coming change in agentic capabilities. The time between a vulnerability being published and being weaponized has collapsed from years to hours.

On adoption, he believes most companies don't need a smarter model. The models are already smart enough. The gap is context they don't absorb - the things an employee who's worked at a company for five years learned by osmosis.

If the frontier stopped advancing today, he thinks it wouldn't meaningfully change the value most are extracting from AI anyway.

author: CathieDWood
quoted_text:
The dead cat continues to bounce.  

What is Bitcoin, 17 years later? 

It’s not great for transactions or smart contracts; the user experience is still intimidating for most, and it’s no longer capturing the public’s imagination. 

If it comes up at the dinner party, it's followed by a hearty “remember that!”

It’s a boring store of value, trusted as that—which is its biggest value. 

It's boring. 

Folks expect bitcoin to be stable and that it’s no longer a way to get rich quick. 

Institutions embracing and accumulating it took $btc from punk rock to Muzak. 

Advocates went from pirates to suits in orange ties, awkwardly sharing cringe memes — just like the cool kids do! 

If Bitcoin were going to reach mass adoption and an important use case, it does better than anyone else, it would have by now. 

Bitcoin feels like the CD in the age of Spotify, the DVD in the age of Netflix  — a bridge technology that folks who invested in “their collection” keep saying is the better experience. 

Perhaps bitcoin is vinyl, cool memories and fun to drag out and put on display, but a technology that served us to get to where we are now.

text:
Four year cycle lows are not an exact science. 

Sometimes it’s a little earlier than normal, sometimes a little later.

The idea that the 4 year cycle “failed” despite Bitcoin dropping below the 200W moving average in H2 of the midterm year seems wrong.

The SPX would often bottom in October, but occasionally it would occur earlier (May) and sometimes later (December)

With Bitcoin, the winning strategy has typically been to just DCA in the second half of the midterm year rather than try and time the exact bottom (something I have reiterated multiple times).
author: benjamincowen
quoted_text:
The most likely low for BTC is October 2026, based on the 4 year cycle.

Under some circumstances it could happen as early as May.

BTC does not have a monopoly on the four-year cycle. 

You can that the S&P 500 has gone through many periods where it bottoms approximately every 4 years. 

Major lows tends to occur in early Q4, but in some cases it occasionally happens in May.

October would be favored if we get multiple week-to-month long countertrend rallies that delay things.

May would be favored if the countertrend rallies just last a few days to a couple weeks, and deeper drawdowns occur sooner.

I favor October over May for now, but as an investor we have to be aware that markets can always evolve in ways we do not expect.

卧槽，JEV 的出现很可能就是自动智能交易的起点。

昨天JEV在AI 圈刷屏，今天 Monad 工程师就用JEV做了一个自动交易机器人。

实时读取 MON/USDC 价格，JEV 不负责写分析报告，也不跟你解释一堆逻辑，它只做最核心的事，判断 Buy 还是 Sell，再给出置信度，然后直接把交易发到 Kuru 的链上订单簿执行。

这一下我突然明白 JEV 为什么要做成一个不会说话的模型了。

交易根本不需要 AI 每 300ms 给你写一篇小作文，它需要的是：

行情进来→判断→下单→新行情→重新判断，而且这一整套循环必须足够快、足够便宜。

而 Monad 现在刚好每 300ms 出一个区块，Kuru 又是链上订单簿。高性能链负责执行，JEV 负责决策，两个东西拼起来，已经有点AI 原生交易系统的味道了。

未来的交易 Agent，不一定需要一个会写研报的超级大模型，它更需要一个能在极低延迟下连续做几百万次判断的大脑。

base:0x940181a94a35a4569e4529a3cdfb74e38fd98631 on the other hand has barely caught any bid with the same tokenized equity tailwind, and the very soon to be $ETH mainnet deployment (maybe more chains? 👀).

text:
Storytelling is finally solved.

Neither ChatGPT nor Claude could solve it because it required long-horizon consistency, and they would just hallucinate consistently.

Sherpa has data on 5.5 billion minutes, which gives it the edge of knowing:

> where the audience gets hooked
> how much surprise each episode can handle
> which twist to hold back, and for how long
> and where the audience drops off

You give it one premise, and it builds a full season where characters, plot threads, and open conflicts stay coherent across 200 to 800 episodes.
author: 0xProtoCon
quoted_text:
Introducing Sherpa: the most advanced fiction writing AI

We accelerated from $250M in ARR to $500M because Sherpa helped increase content production by 1200% in 1 year

Sherpa was trained on 5.5B hours of playtime with minute by minute dynamic retention data.

550K+ creators have produced 2.6M hours of content annualised using it

Pocket FM is like Netflix for audio-only dramas, with our own pool of one-person studios.

10% of eligible writers on Pocket FM make >$200K
One blockbuster produced >$100M in revenue
3 writers have become millionaires in <2 yrs

We built Sherpa to enable anyone to make >$1M by writing world-class fiction stories:

1. The Idea: Drop a 1-2 sentence concept. Sherpa interrogates it like a veteran editor on tension, stakes, and psychology
2. World & Characters: It builds out the complete lore, tone, and character psychologies
3. Sub-Plot planning: Breaks the premise into arcs, arcs into episodes, and episodes into scenes
4. Scene-by-Scene Generation: Outlines and drafts entire episodes, with you able to steer, rewrite, or override anytime
5. Editorial Review: Stress-tests every draft for pacing, engagement drop-offs, prose, and coherence before it locks
6. One-Tap Production: Pick a voice, convert to audio drama, and publish directly to Pocket FM’s millions of listeners
7. Global Scale & Monetization: Revenue-share on performance, with automatic localization so you earn across international markets

Test Sherpa for free here: https://t.co/R39M5o0Miz
_____________________________________________

Generic LLMs fail at serialized fiction because they lack a long-horizon narrative reward function.

Sherpa solves this through three core technical leaps:

1. Narrative World Model (State Tracking & Retrieval): Context windows degrade over long runs. Sherpa constructs an evolving semantic knowledge graph tracking character states, secrets, and plot dependencies. High-speed retrieval surfaces exact context on demand, maintaining zero continuity decay across hundreds of episodes

2. Hierarchical Story Planner: When writing a 500-episode story like Naruto, you need to plan 100s of sub plots. Rather than generating linearly, Sherpa decomposes narrative across discrete levels: season -> arc -> sequence -> episode -> scene.

Rather than generating everything upfront, like a generic LLM, Sherpa uses progressive planning and dynamic replanning. As the story evolves, it identifies what changed, traces the downstream impact, and replans only the affected parts.

3. Prose Engine (Trained on series' retention data): LLMs write robotically, but serial fiction needs emotion, tension, pacing, and dialogue that sounds like real people.

Sherpa's Prose Engine was designed specifically for storytelling. It was built on 1B+ tokens of Pocket's own stories, trained by learning from what listeners engage with, where they drop off, and what keeps them hooked.

Feedback is taken from specialized evaluator models that measure every scene against a 40-item checklist. (Evaluator models were benchmarked against human reviewers and matched them 80–90% of the time.)
_______________________________________________

Owning distribution and creation puts us in a very unique spot.
More shows -> More data -> Sherpa becomes better -> more creator success -> more creators -> more shows

Pocket FM has already seen one $100M IP. I believe Sherpa will soon lead to dozens of single-person studios creating billion-dollar shows.

Most people are scared of AI but I think it'll unlock more human creativity, help creators earn more, and bring the next great IPs to life. This will create millions of jobs and new income streams.

text:
Jev的产品和宣发都很顶尖，从冷启动、创作者模版、相关群体的有机互动，都值得学习下，整个故事还要从创始人包装说起。

一个1500粉的号，两年没发声，9月15日一句 “After co-inventing ChatGPT” 把stealth产品、新模型类别、DCVC领投的4000万融资一次性打出去，主帖收获两千万+浏览。创始人履历确实很硬，InstructGPT核心作者，但是确实话术也做了包装，RLHF不是他一个人发明的，与此同时，ChatGPT也没有所谓的发明人。

1/ 宣发并非自然爆发，而是高投入冷启动

https://t.co/LKmViRGJtg接了内容策略、发布包和当天seeding。创始人号从约1500涨到9万+，官号从200到6万+。宣发预算打满后，在发布后第一小时就铺天盖地把工程师和founder们时间线填满了Jev内容。

冷启动种子是买的，但后面几千万浏览是算法主动承接。一场大约8–12万美元的发布战役，撬出平均launch二十多倍的曝光，ROI可以说非常好了。

2/ 创作者侧的模版化生产

用心留意的朋友，应该会观察到Jev相关内容反复出现同一套结构：先一句“LLM写字 / Jev做决定”，再塞工单路由、风控、agent选工具，最后一段屏幕录像。Mario、Doom、Browser Use找航班，全是同一套演示语法。

还有一句比RLCD好传播一百倍的产品句：输出token定价为零。创作者不需要理解训练方法，复述“$0.042/M输入、输出免费、70–500ms”就够了。

模版的作用是让技术观众在不同账号上反复撞见同一个可理解的差异。看起来像有机讨论，但底层是可复制、低成本的叙事零件。

3/ 第一批技术群体跟上，铺量后飞轮效应出现

英文圈先行发动，Vercel高管公开测分类任务，有人开源约束解码复刻，有人把Jev接进browser agent。三天内社区冒出LiteLLM透传、Instructor预设、Pi路由插件、jev-browser、两个MCP server，中文圈接着快速承接。

而真实用户，吐槽也不少，比如有人拿到key之后发现打游戏泛化不如Astra，强项是快和便宜，这种帖比重复200x口号更真实可信。

4/ 渠道接棒，平台开始借它给自己引流

9/16 Vercel AI Gateway上架，官方称付费团队24小时渗透约13%，历史最快，随即把Jev免到9月25日

9/18 OpenRouter上架 typesafe/jev-1.13，只走Decisions端点，chat/completions直接拒绝

这些平台在用当下最快冷启动的模型给自己的Gateway获客，飞轮效应进一步加速。

5/ 链路复盘

创始人给一句可核验的身份，适当包装

产品差异压成对比句和一个反常识定价，让创作者能直接套模版

发布当天只服务第一小时，剩下交给算法

发动顶级平台一起 co-PR，启动互利飞轮

Jev官网很丑，但是文档和调用路径非常清楚。团队思路非常清晰，知道转化不来自官网，而在创始人发帖、Gateway合作和文档。

text:
Meaningful infrastructure takes time to build.

The current market moves fast.

Attention shifts in hours, and expectations often move even faster.

We’re building Superstables differently.

Phase 0 is already shipped: the Superstables Index is live, with 1,900+ payable services indexed and continuously probed.

Now the team is actively building V1: the Router.

V1 takes Superstables from discovery to execution:
→ discover a payable service
→ check what it costs
→ obtain explicit wallet authorization
→ route the payment across supported rails
→ sign locally
→ execute the payment
→ verify the result and receipt

We’re also building the SDK, CLI and MCP interfaces, wallet integrations, spending controls, payment reconciliation and recovery infrastructure that sit around that flow.

The payment path will go through an independent security audit before the public V1 release. After that, the roadmap continues.

Router → Control Plane → Trust.

We’re not trying to build something that holds attention for a few days.

We’re building infrastructure we expect to be working on for a long time.

One milestone at a time.

https://t.co/8d8qCHfuol

Not Financial Advice.

quoted_text:
Vitalik on AI-assisted formal verification of entire programs

Reading it with my pea brain, several parts of @VitalikButerin's post actually line up with what @theInterfold is building? Basically using FHE + ZK proofs + threshold decryption so private inputs can produce a shared, checkable result without a trusted operator

1. "for many of the most critical components - message-passing protocols, sandboxes, cryptography like SNARKs and FHE - the asymmetry is real.”

Interfold’s stack: FHE computes on encrypted bids/votes, ZK proofs show the computation was done correctly, and threshold cryptography so no single party can decrypt alone

2. “If AI can prove Navier-Stokes and FLT, then AI can prove the statement ‘this program is secure’ as a mathematical theorem. Even if the program is very complicated.”

Interfold’s pitch is that the program (Encrypted Execution Environment) should satisfy a precise claim: private inputs in, only the permitted output out, and a proof that the result is correct (“prove the program is secure”)

3. “the definition is a much smaller attack surface than the implementation. Verifying that the definition is adequate is a much more tractable task than scanning over the code directly… Definitions are also additive.”

Interfold keeps repeating a small set of definitions rather than “just encrypt it”: private inputs, verifiable outputs, no trusted hardware, no single party with decryption authority. Read their latest blog post on sealed-bid auction https://t.co/yFmZaw3gx9

4. “There is no future for blockchains - especially blockchains with scalability and privacy - without doing this. We need to make software actually secure.”

Interfold is a privacy-and-coordination layer on Ethereum: on-chain eligibility/proofs, encrypted execution off that, threshold-decrypted public result. Vitalik already said that Interfold is the generalized MACI design he had been asking people to build (https://t.co/dV8YMdkBs3)

5. “What if the adversary hacked the server?”, “How did you learn which public key belongs to the recipient?”, “Are you hiding the size of the payload?”

Interfold aims to solve who has authority to decrypt, whether the result is complete, and whether the process can be coerced

quoted_text:
一切都是为了健康，为自己，家人和团队负责。
早上醒来，就处理几个同事（美国、国内、香港）的要求，只简单吃了点玉米、土豆、和一个希腊酸奶，加奇异果。

中午空肚吃姜黄、通心血管，而午餐是三只鸡蛋，水果和酸奶，喝一壶柠檬热水，然后，就是要吃的CoQ-10m 、Omega 3、蔓越莓丸、肠道益生菌、维生素B群、蓝莓素和葉黃素、锌片和NAD丸，当然还有补肝的。

下午二十分钟power nap， 下午第一个会3点，让自己在脑袋最清晰的时间，看书30分钟。

昨天特意去深圳做正骨包括了推拿、针灸加艾灸，2-3小时，老中医负责，在香港几乎找不到这么优秀有经验的，消除疲劳，筋骨的舒络，激发免疫力。

中午吃五指毛桃高压锅炖的走地鸡（优质蛋白），地瓜叶（高纤维、营养丰富），带鱼（优质蛋白），一部分三种米组合的米饭，生地熟地黑豆汤 （去湿），还有凉瓜排骨 （清凉祛毒）。

下午，把会都改期，去了做脸部护理，大概两个小时，躺着听柴可夫斯基，休息够后，和两位企业家，去了打兵乓球，两个小时，其实很出汗的，自己从正拍，过渡去横拍。

晚上，简单吃了，回了部分电邮，洗澡，就尝试睡了。

其实peptide、Retinol、维他命水都很重要，男女通用。

对于动刀的医美，其实不大赞成，要是要做运动，特别是力量训练，至少要有一定的线条，倒三角。

植发是应该做的，马斯克也做了，有很大的效果。至于拉皮，有可能倒某一个年纪会尝试做，至于眼枪是可以考虑，微创去眼袋，可以考虑，其他真的要三思。

简单的护肤、搽防晒、清洁，睡眠，保湿，会把你和同龄人，甩开10年甚至以上！

一切都是为了健康，愉悦自己。

感恩，我有两个亲姐姐把我照顾的很好。

以后找机会聊护肤和穿着，大家多学习陈传多！

太多人写Near了，我就简单总结下NEAR 最近到底在干什么？其实就四件事：

1.做全链交易所

核心是 NEAR Intents + https://t.co/GtWHwsEXfG。

用户不用管哪条链、怎么跨桥、Gas 从哪来，只说自己想换成什么资产，后台由 Solver 自动找最优路径完成跨链交易和结算。

2.做隐私交易

NEAR 把 Confidential Intents 推到了前台，隐藏资金来源、交易路径和钱包关联。现在连 Hyperliquid 永续都接进来了，35+ 条链的资产可以直接进去做 Perp。

3.搞期权式空投（这个比较创新）

NEAR@3.33 不是普通空投，先给你锁定奖励，只有机密 TVL 和 NEAR 价格同时达到条件，才能 1:1 解锁成 NEAR。说白了，就是把用户增长、TVL 和币价绑在了一起。

4.给 AI Agent 做结算后台

NEAR AI、Shade Agents、机密 GPU、Agent 支付都在往一个方向走：以后 AI 自己持有密钥、跨链交易、调用工具、支付稳定币，NEAR 在后台负责签名、隐私和结算。

NEAR这个团队一直会搞事情，这次从公链华丽转身，彻底改变了方向和产品形态，这不是一般公链就能做到的。

a16z-Backed Layer 1 Project Linera Announces Shutdown

The Linera team announced on Discord that it is ceasing operations immediately due to insufficient funding. Its token sale on Sonar attracted nearly $900,000 in commitments but missed the minimum threshold, and all contributions have been refunded. Emergency funding efforts also failed. Linera is winding down its app and Discord community. Points balances will remain on record, but no future benefits are guaranteed. The team still hopes to complete the protocol and launch applications, though no timeline is available.

Founded by former Meta researcher Mathieu Baudet, Linera raised approximately $12 million across two rounds in 2022 and 2023, with a16z participating in both. Other investors included Borderless Capital, GSR, Matrixport Ventures, and Flow Traders.

1// Each successful run is distilled into procedure nodes: the conditions under which a workflow applies, the actions the agent took, and the outcomes it produced. 

2// When a task arrives, Memorable retrieves relevant nodes and constructs an ordered path through them.
Because procedures can be composed, the agent can execute workflows that no previous agent has run end to end. This essentially turns agent reasoning into a graph search problem. 

3// The Memorable CLI is live across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Claude Cowork. Memorable is also deployed in @garrytan's GBrain, GStack, and YC's QM Harness.

4// The long-term goal: systems agents whose operational competence compounds across sessions.
